en.title: Their Hearts Tremble and Their Faith Increases
en.excerpt: Faith grows through reciting and reflecting on the verses, and its fruit is a heart that relies on its Lord alone.

body.text: In this verse Allah paints the portrait of the true believer: a heart that is humbled when its Lord is mentioned, faith that increases whenever the verses are recited to it, and all of this crowned with reliance upon Allah alone in every matter.
إِنَّمَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَجِلَتۡ قُلُوبُهُمۡ وَإِذَا تُلِيَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتُهُۥ زَادَتۡهُمۡ إِيمَٰنٗا وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ

Faith is not something static; it grows and flourishes through the Qur'an and remembrance, and it weakens through heedlessness and turning away. Whoever wishes to measure the state of his heart should look: does it stir when it hears the verses? Does he find in them an increase in certainty and tranquility?

Keep a fixed daily portion of reflective recitation, even if it is small, and pause at the verse that touches your heart. The fruit of that is trust in Allah that lets you approach your affairs relying on Him rather than on yourself.

en.title: As Though It Had Not Flourished Yesterday
en.excerpt: The adornment of this world is like crops that turned green and then became a harvested field; so do not build your heart on what fades away.

body.text: In this verse Allah strikes a remarkable parable for the life of this world: rain comes down and the plants of the earth mingle with it, until, when the earth has taken on its adornment and its people think they have full power over it, Allah's command comes to it and He makes it a harvested field, as though it had not flourished the day before.

إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا كَمَاءٍ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَبَاتُ الْأَرْضِ مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ النَّاسُ وَالْأَنْعَامُ حَتَّىٰ إِذَا أَخَذَتِ الْأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَهَا وَازَّيَّنَتْ وَظَنَّ أَهْلُهَا أَنَّهُمْ قَادِرُونَ عَلَيْهَا أَتَاهَا أَمْرُنَا لَيْلًا أَوْ نَهَارًا فَجَعَلْنَاهَا حَصِيدًا كَأَنْ لَمْ تَغْنَ بِالْأَمْسِ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

How much a person's life resembles these crops: he gathers, adorns and feels secure, and then all of it passes away in a moment. The wise person does not belittle Allah's blessings, but neither does he make them the goal of his heart; he enjoys them with gratitude and sends ahead from them for what will last. Reflect on how the verse ends, «for a people who give thought»: the parable benefits only the one who pauses and reflects on it.

en.title: Whoever Fulfils His Covenant and Fears Allah
en.excerpt: Keeping one's promises is a sign of God-consciousness and a path to Allah's love.

body.text: Allah pairs the fulfilment of covenants with taqwa (God-consciousness), and ends the verse with His love for the God-conscious. The commitment a person makes with his Lord and with people is not a passing word; it is a trust he will be asked about, and a great door to drawing near to Allah.
بَلَىٰ مَنْ أَوْفَىٰ بِعَهْدِهِ وَاتَّقَىٰ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ

When you promise someone an appointment, a task, or the return of money, make keeping that promise an act of worship by which you draw near to Allah, and never belittle a commitment however small it seems. Trust between people is built from these small promises that are kept, and it collapses when they are broken. Whoever is unable to keep his word because of an unforeseen excuse should hasten to apologise and explain, for that is part of complete truthfulness and of safeguarding people's rights.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 76

en.title: Let Me Die a Muslim and Join Me with the Righteous
en.excerpt: At the height of honour and power, Yusuf asked his Lord for a good ending and was not distracted by what he had been given.

body.text: After he had been reunited with his family and attained a lofty position, Yusuf (peace be upon him) did not ask for more of this world. Rather, he acknowledged Allah's blessings upon him of authority and knowledge, then turned to the Originator of the heavens and the earth, asking Him to let him die in submission (as a Muslim) and to join him with the righteous.

رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ الْمُلْكِ وَعَلَّمْتَنِي مِنْ تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ ۚ فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَنْتَ وَلِيِّي فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ ۖ تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ

The true blessing is that the heart stays attached to Allah in times of ease just as it is attached to Him in times of hardship. When the world comes to you, remember that the ending is what matters most, and make it part of your constant supplication that Allah keeps you firm upon Islam until you meet Him, and that He gathers you with the righteous in this world and the Hereafter.

en.title: With Allah Alone Is Knowledge of the Hour
en.excerpt: No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow; so work today and entrust tomorrow to the One who knows it.

body.text: Surah Luqman closes with a verse that mentions matters of the unseen whose knowledge Allah has kept to Himself: knowledge of the Hour, the sending down of rain, what is in the wombs, what a soul will earn tomorrow, and the land in which it will die. It then ends by stating that Allah is All-Knowing, All-Aware.

إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا فِي الْأَرْحَامِ ۖ وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ مَاذَا تَكْسِبُ غَدًا ۖ وَمَا تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ

His words «what it will earn tomorrow» teach you that tomorrow is not in your hands. So do not postpone repentance and good deeds on the pretext that there is plenty of time, and do not carry the worry of the future as if you owned it. Do what you can in your day, and ask Allah for good in what comes after it.

In «in what land it will die» there is a gentle reminder that one's appointed term is written in its place and time; fear does not bring it forward and eagerness does not delay it. So live ready to meet Allah, at peace in the knowledge that all your affairs are in the hand of the All-Knowing, All-Aware.

en.title: Prayer Restrains from Indecency
en.excerpt: A living prayer leaves its mark on one's conduct and holds the one who prays back from what is shameful.

body.text: In this verse the Qur'an links reciting the Book with establishing the prayer, and then explains the effect of prayer on a servant's life: it is not a set of movements performed and then forgotten, but a light that accompanies the worshipper after he ends it with the salam.
ٱتۡلُ مَآ أُوحِيَ إِلَيۡكَ مِنَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۖ إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنۡهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلۡفَحۡشَآءِ وَٱلۡمُنكَرِۗ وَلَذِكۡرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكۡبَرُۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تَصۡنَعُونَ

If you find yourself praying yet see no effect of the prayer on your tongue and your dealings, examine how present your heart is in it. The greater the humility, the stronger the connection, and the stronger the connection, the weaker the hold of sin over the soul. The verse ends by saying that «the remembrance of Allah is greater», and that He knows what we do; being mindful that He sees you in private and in public is among the greatest aids to remaining upright after every prayer.

en.title: Be Grateful to Me and to Your Parents
en.excerpt: Allah joined gratitude to parents with gratitude to Him, so honouring them became an act of worship, not a courtesy.

body.text: Allah reminds man of the hardship his mother endured as she carried him in weakness upon weakness, then nursed and raised him, and He places gratitude to parents right after gratitude to Him, so that a person realises that behind every blessing he enjoys there is a tender hand that toiled for his sake.
وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ بِوَالِدَيْهِ حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ وَهْنًا عَلَىٰ وَهْنٍ وَفِصَالُهُ فِي عَامَيْنِ أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيْكَ إِلَيَّ الْمَصِيرُ

Gratitude to parents is not a word said on special occasions; it is a daily character: to ask after them, to lighten their burdens, to mention their virtue in front of your children, and to pray for them in your prostration. The verse's ending, «to Me is the final return», reminds you that this kindness is preserved with Allah, and the servant will meet it on the day he returns to Him. So make the most of their lives, and do not put off a visit, a call or a gift.

en.title: Do Not Relate Your Dream to Your Brothers
en.excerpt: Among the wisdom of Yaqub (peace be upon him): some blessings are protected by keeping them private until Allah permits them to appear.

body.text: Yusuf (peace be upon him) relates a wondrous dream to his father, and the wise father receives it with quiet joy and merciful advice: to keep this glad tiding to himself and not tell his brothers about it, knowing what a blessing might stir up in some souls.

إِذْ قَالَ يُوسُفُ لِأَبِيهِ يَا أَبَتِ إِنِّي رَأَيْتُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كَوْكَبًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ رَأَيْتُهُمْ لِي سَاجِدِينَ
قَالَ يَا بُنَيَّ لَا تَقْصُصْ رُؤْيَاكَ عَلَىٰ إِخْوَتِكَ فَيَكِيدُوا لَكَ كَيْدًا ۖ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ لِلْإِنْسَانِ عَدُوٌّ مُبِينٌ

Not every good thing that comes to you is best announced to everyone. The believer thanks Allah for His blessing and speaks of it in its proper place, but he keeps to himself what he fears might stir envy or resentment in hearts, out of mercy to himself and to others. The verse also holds a beautiful lesson in upbringing: the father listens to his son, shares his joy, then guides him gently and reminds him that «Satan is to man a clear enemy», protecting the family from the causes of division before they arise.

en.title: He Would Not Change a Favour He Had Bestowed
en.excerpt: Blessings endure through gratitude and uprightness, and are taken away only when what is within souls changes.

body.text: This verse reveals a constant divine law among nations and individuals: Allah does not remove a blessing He has bestowed upon a people until they themselves change what is within them of faith, obedience and gratitude.
ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَمۡ يَكُ مُغَيِّرٗا نِّعۡمَةً أَنۡعَمَهَا عَلَىٰ قَوۡمٍ حَتَّىٰ يُغَيِّرُواْ مَا بِأَنفُسِهِمۡ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٞ

A blessing is a trust, and it is preserved by thanking the One who bestowed it and using it in obedience to Him. If a person sees a blessing diminishing around him, let him begin by examining himself before blaming circumstances and people; the change required may well be within him.

The verse's ending, «All-Hearing, All-Knowing», is a reminder that Allah knows what goes on in hearts and what tongues utter; neither the sincerity of the grateful nor the heedlessness of the heedless is hidden from Him. So strive to make what is within you a cause for the blessing to last, not for it to vanish.

en.title: The Enduring Good Deeds
en.excerpt: Wealth and children are a passing adornment; what truly remains for you is righteous deeds.

body.text: After Allah likened this world to vegetation that became dry stubble scattered by the winds, He mentioned the dearest things people cling to, wealth and children, describing them as the adornment of the life of this world. He then directed hearts to what is better with Him in reward and better to hope for.

وَٱضۡرِبۡ لَهُم مَّثَلَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَٱخۡتَلَطَ بِهِۦ نَبَاتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَأَصۡبَحَ هَشِيمٗا تَذۡرُوهُ ٱلرِّيَٰحُۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ مُّقۡتَدِرًا
ٱلۡمَالُ وَٱلۡبَنُونَ زِينَةُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَٱلۡبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ خَيۡرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابٗا وَخَيۡرٌ أَمَلٗا

Adornment is beautiful but does not last, whereas the enduring good deeds, remembrance, prayer, charity and a good word, are a balance that the winds cannot scatter. So set aside a share of these enduring deeds every day, even if small, and be good to your family and in your wealth with a sincere intention, so that the adornment itself is transformed into a lasting deed.

en.title: From What You Love
en.excerpt: A person does not attain the fullness of righteousness until he gives generously from what his soul is attached to.

body.text: The verse sets a precise measure for righteousness: giving is not handing over what you have lost interest in, but spending from what your soul loves and holds dear, and then being at peace knowing that Allah is fully aware of everything you spend, whether little or much.
لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّىٰ تُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ ۚ وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ

Try choosing, for your charity or your gift, something you truly love rather than your surplus. This trains the soul in generosity and is a victory over the stinginess hidden within it. Remember that giving is not only money; it may be time you cherish or effort you spend for others. And since Allah knows what you spend, you have no need for people to see you or praise you; it is enough for you that nothing is ever lost with Him.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 92

en.title: I Only Complain of My Grief and Sorrow to Allah
en.excerpt: Complaining to Allah does not contradict patience; rather, it is the door to relief and rest for the troubled heart.

body.text: When the grief of Yaqub (peace be upon him) over the loss of his two sons grew intense and those around him blamed him, he told them that he poured out his grief and sorrow only to Allah alone, and that he knew from Allah's mercy and gentleness what they did not know. So his hope stayed alive despite the length of the trial.
قَالَ إِنَّمَا أَشْكُو بَثِّي وَحُزْنِي إِلَى اللَّهِ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ

When your chest feels heavy, do not lock your worry inside, nor scatter it among people as complaint and grumbling. Instead, take it to Allah in your prostration and supplication, for He knows your state best and is most able to remove it. Make good expectation of Him your companion, for complaining to Him is worship, and waiting with hope is beautiful patience.

en.title: The Ever-Living, the Sustainer of All
en.excerpt: Your Lord is overtaken by neither drowsiness nor sleep; He watches over your affairs at every moment, even while you sleep.

body.text: A mighty verse that acquaints the servant with his Lord: there is no god but He, Ever-Living with perfect life, Self-Subsisting and Sustainer of all else, overtaken by neither drowsiness nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, His knowledge encompasses everything, and preserving them does not weary Him.

ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٞ وَلَا نَوۡمٞۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيۡءٖ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ

When you reflect on «neither drowsiness overtakes Him», your fears subside. You sleep, you are heedless and you are weak, while your Lord is not unaware of you for the blink of an eye. So entrust to Him what you cannot manage, and sleep at peace after you have done your part of effort and supplication.

In His words «and preserving them does not weary Him» there is a lesson in trust: if preserving the heavens and the earth is no burden to Him, then protecting you, your family and your provision is easier still. Make this verse the companion of your day, and recall its meanings morning and evening.

en.title: Establish Prayer for My Remembrance
en.excerpt: The purpose of prayer is for the servant to remember his Lord; when remembrance is absent, its spirit is absent.

body.text: In the first moment of intimate address to Musa (peace be upon him), the command to worship Allah alone came paired with establishing the prayer, and its purpose was made clear in a single phrase: «for My remembrance». Prayer is an appointment in which the remembrance of Allah is renewed in the servant's heart.
إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ لِذِكْرِي

So give your prayer a preparation that readies your heart: an unhurried ablution, calm steps to the place of prayer, and a moment of silence before the opening takbir in which you remember before Whom you are about to stand. Whoever Allah helps in this finds prayer a rest rather than a burden, and comes to await the next prayer with longing, rather than performing it in haste just to be done with it.

en.title: Accompany Them in This World with Kindness
en.excerpt: Even when there is disagreement over the greatest of matters, parents keep their right to kind companionship.

body.text: The verse speaks of parents who strive to push their child towards what does not please Allah. It commands him not to obey them in that, and at the same time commands him to accompany them in this world with kindness and good treatment, without cutting them off or being harsh.

وَإِنْ جَاهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰ أَنْ تُشْرِكَ بِي مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا ۖ وَصَاحِبْهُمَا فِي الدُّنْيَا مَعْرُوفًا ۖ وَاتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّ ۚ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ

Disagreeing with one's parents over an opinion or a way of life does not permit harshness or abandonment; gentleness, visiting, serving them and a kind word remain their right however much viewpoints differ. Herein is a great lesson for every home: to distinguish between the position and the relationship, so that we hold firmly to the truth with good manners, preserve affection with patience, and keep our parents' hearts always open to us.

en.title: So Patience Is Most Fitting
en.excerpt: When the painful news came, Yaqub did not panic; he chose beautiful patience and sought Allah's help.

body.text: Yusuf's brothers return with his shirt stained with false blood. Yaqub (peace be upon him) realises that there is a scheme behind it, yet he neither explodes in anger nor despairs; rather, he speaks his timeless words and entrusts the whole matter to Allah.
وَجَاءُوا عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِ بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ ۚ قَالَ بَلْ سَوَّلَتْ لَكُمْ أَنْفُسُكُمْ أَمْرًا ۖ فَصَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ ۖ وَاللَّهُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ

Beautiful patience is patience without complaint to people and without resentment of fate, while the heart remains alive with hope. The believer may feel pain and grief, yet he restrains his tongue and his actions and turns towards Allah. His words «and Allah is the One whose help is sought» teach us that patience itself needs help from Allah, so the servant does not rely on his own strength alone, but asks his Lord to help him bear what has befallen him.

en.title: Do Not Grieve; Indeed Allah Is with Us
en.excerpt: Allah's being with His allies sends down tranquility in the most frightening and constricted of situations.

body.text: The verse recalls a moment when fear reached its peak: two men in a cave with their pursuers all around them, and yet the word on the tongue was «Indeed Allah is with us». So Allah sent down His tranquility and supported him with soldiers that were not seen.

إِلَّا تَنْصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ اللَّهُ إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ثَانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَاحِبِهِ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا ۖ فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَيَّدَهُ بِجُنُودٍ لَمْ تَرَوْهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا السُّفْلَىٰ ۗ وَكَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيَا ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ

Victory may come from where the servant does not expect, and through means he cannot see. When your situation becomes tight and the means grow few, remember that Allah is with you through His knowledge, His help and His support, and that this companionship is enough to drive grief from your heart.

In hours of anxiety, repeat the meaning of «Indeed Allah is with us», take whatever means you can, and then leave the outcomes to the One in whose hand is the whole affair, for He is Almighty and never overcome, All-Wise and never puts anything except in its proper place.

en.title: It Leaves Nothing Small or Great
en.excerpt: The record of your deeds omits nothing; so fill it with what you would love to see on the Day of Resurrection.

body.text: The verse depicts the scene of the Book being laid open on the Day of Resurrection, when the wrongdoers see their records and are fearful of what is in them, astonished at how precisely they were counted: nothing small or great has been left out, and they find everything they did present before them.

وَوُضِعَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ فَتَرَى ٱلۡمُجۡرِمِينَ مُشۡفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَٰوَيۡلَتَنَا مَالِ هَٰذَا ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةٗ وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّآ أَحۡصَىٰهَاۚ وَوَجَدُواْ مَا عَمِلُواْ حَاضِرٗاۗ وَلَا يَظۡلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدٗا

We often belittle a word, a glance or a shortcoming, thinking it will fade with the days, yet the verse reminds us that it is present, waiting for us. Likewise, a small good deed is also preserved and never lost. So do not take any sin lightly however small, nor neglect any kindness however little, and find reassurance in the verse's ending: «and your Lord does not wrong anyone».

en.title: Do Not Deprive People of Their Due
en.excerpt: Fairness in measure and weight extends to giving people all their rights in full.

body.text: Shu'ayb commands his people to give full measure and weight with justice, and forbids them from short-changing people of what is theirs, counting that as spreading corruption in the land. Cheating in dealings is no small matter; it is a flaw that destroys trust and harms the whole of society.
وَيَا قَوْمِ أَوْفُوا الْمِكْيَالَ وَالْمِيزَانَ بِالْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا النَّاسَ أَشْيَاءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ

Short-changing enters many matters besides trade: underpaying a worker his wage, belittling a colleague's effort, or ignoring someone's favour to you. Make it your habit to give everyone their due in full, in money, in words and in appreciation, for fairness is a character that sets the earth right and sows love.

en.title: And Say: My Lord, Increase Me in Knowledge
en.excerpt: Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to ask Him for more knowledge, for it is a provision one can never do without.

body.text: In this verse Allah guides His Prophet ﷺ to be patient in receiving the revelation and not to hasten in reciting it before it is complete, then teaches him a short, comprehensive supplication in which he asks his Lord for an increase in beneficial knowledge.
فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ ۗ وَلَا تَعْجَلْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُقْضَىٰ إِلَيْكَ وَحْيُهُ ۖ وَقُلْ رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا

Beneficial knowledge has no limit, and however much of it a person attains, he still needs more. So keep this supplication on your tongue before reading, before studying and before every lesson, and seek knowledge that brings you closer to Allah and sets your deeds right. And remember that patience and careful verification are among the manners of the seeker of knowledge.

en.title: He Is the First and the Last
en.excerpt: Everything has a beginning and an end except Allah; so attach yourself to the Everlasting and do not surrender your heart to what perishes.

body.text: Four majestic names in a single verse: the First, before whom there is nothing; the Last, after whom there is nothing; the Manifest and the Hidden. It then closes by stating that He has full knowledge of everything, so nothing minute or great escapes His knowledge.
هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

When you know that your Lord is «the First and the Last», you realise that everything besides Him is transient and will pass: wealth, position, health and people. So do not build your happiness on what perishes; build it on your bond with the Everlasting, glory be to Him, and do your deeds for His sake, for what is done for Him remains.

The verse's ending, «and He has full knowledge of everything», gives you calm in moments of injustice and obscurity: what is hidden from people of your intention and effort is not hidden from Him, so work for Him and do not wait for anyone else's testimony. The more you remember His all-encompassing knowledge, the lighter people's opinion becomes to you, and the purer your deeds become from showing off.

en.title: The Month of Ramadan in Which the Qur'an Was Revealed
en.excerpt: Ramadan is the month of the Qur'an before it is the month of fasting, so give the Mushaf an ample share of it.

body.text: Allah introduced the month of Ramadan by the greatest thing that took place in it, the revelation of the Qur'an as guidance for mankind, and only then mentioned fasting. This indicates that fasting and the Qur'an go hand in hand: one refines the heart so that it can receive the other.

شَهۡرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ هُدٗى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٖ مِّنَ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ وَٱلۡفُرۡقَانِۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهۡرَ فَلۡيَصُمۡهُۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٖ فَعِدَّةٞ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡيُسۡرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلۡعُسۡرَ وَلِتُكۡمِلُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ

The same verse reminds us that Allah «intends ease for you»; worship in Islam is a mercy, not a hardship sought for its own sake, and whoever knows this approaches it with a tranquil soul. The verse ends with magnifying Allah and giving thanks for guidance, so make your fasting and your recitation a practical thanks to Allah, and set yourself a daily portion of the Qur'an that you keep up in Ramadan and continue after it.

en.title: O My Son, Establish Prayer
en.excerpt: Luqman's advice is a complete method of upbringing: prayer that connects the son to his Lord, setting people right, and patience along the way.

body.text: Luqman continues advising his son, moving from affirming the oneness of Allah to action: establishing prayer, enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, and being patient with whatever befalls him in doing so. He concludes that these are among the matters requiring firm resolve, which need determination and steadfastness.
يَا بُنَيَّ أَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ وَأْمُرْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَانْهَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَاصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا أَصَابَكَ ۖ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ

Successful upbringing is not content with commands; it builds in the child a connection with Allah, a sense of responsibility towards those around him, and the ability to be patient when he grows tired or is let down. So make your conversations with your children a calm, gradual dialogue like Luqman's, and be a role model for them in what you call them to, for children learn with their eyes before their ears.

en.title: He Said: I Seek Refuge in Allah
en.excerpt: In the most intense moment of temptation, Yusuf turned to Allah and remembered kindness and loyalty.

body.text: The doors were locked and temptation pressed hard upon a young stranger in a house not his own. His first response was to seek refuge in Allah, then to recall the right of the one who had treated him well, and then to declare that wrongdoers never succeed.
وَرَاوَدَتْهُ الَّتِي هُوَ فِي بَيْتِهَا عَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَغَلَّقَتِ الْأَبْوَابَ وَقَالَتْ هَيْتَ لَكَ ۚ قَالَ مَعَاذَ اللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهُ رَبِّي أَحْسَنَ مَثْوَايَ ۖ إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ

The believer's first weapon against enticement is to turn sincerely to Allah: «I seek refuge in Allah». Protection from sin does not come from willpower alone, but from holding fast to Allah and seeking His help. Yusuf (peace be upon him) then adds a moral dimension: loyalty to the one who honoured him. Sin is a betrayal of Allah first, and then of whoever trusted you and treated you well; whoever keeps that in mind finds it easier to give up what his soul desires.

en.title: Nothing Will Befall Us Except What Allah Has Decreed for Us
en.excerpt: Certainty that every matter is written with Allah frees the heart from anxiety and strengthens reliance on Him.

body.text: This verse teaches a phrase that fills the heart with steadfastness: whatever befalls the believer is only what Allah has written for him, and Allah is his Protector and Helper, so upon Him alone should one rely.
قُلْ لَنْ يُصِيبَنَا إِلَّا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَنَا هُوَ مَوْلَانَا ۚ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ

Reflecting on His words «decreed for us» reveals that what Allah ordains for His believing servant is in reality for him and not against him, even if it appears harsh on the surface, because behind it lies wisdom and mercy from his Protector.

So if you fear the future or are troubled by what has not yet happened, do what is within your ability, then entrust the matter to Allah and be at peace. What has been written for you will not pass you by, and nothing will befall you except what the All-Wise, the Most Merciful has decreed.

en.title: Let Him Do Righteous Deeds
en.excerpt: Two conditions for a deed to be accepted: that it be righteous, and that it be sincerely for Allah alone.

body.text: Surah Al-Kahf closes with this comprehensive verse: whoever hopes to meet his Lord should combine two things, to do righteous deeds and to associate no one in the worship of his Lord. Hoping for that meeting is not a wish to be voiced, but action and sincerity.

قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ بَشَرٞ مِّثۡلُكُمۡ يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَآ إِلَٰهُكُمۡ إِلَٰهٞ وَٰحِدٞۖ فَمَن كَانَ يَرۡجُواْ لِقَآءَ رَبِّهِۦ فَلۡيَعۡمَلۡ عَمَلٗا صَٰلِحٗا وَلَا يُشۡرِكۡ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِۦٓ أَحَدَۢا

Sincerity is a secret between the servant and his Lord that no one else sees. Before you begin any deed, ask yourself: for whom am I doing this? And if the love of praise enters your heart, do not abandon the deed; rather, renew and correct your intention. Let your hope of meeting your Lord be what drives you, for whoever is truthful in hoping for that meeting prepares for it.

en.title: Be Patient, for Allah Does Not Let Be Lost
en.excerpt: Your patience in obedience and with people's harm is excellence whose reward is never lost with Allah.

body.text: A short verse that combines a command and a promise: a command to be patient, and a promise that Allah does not let the reward of those who do good be lost. Patience here is part of excellence (ihsan), and every moment of endurance for the sake of the truth is preserved with a Generous Lord from whom nothing is hidden.
وَاصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ

When you bear a hurtful word or the hardship of a good deed with patience, do not think your patience has gone to waste; Allah has guaranteed its reward. This certainty makes patience lighter on the soul, transforming it from exhausting suppression into an act of worship whose doer awaits its reward. So when your chest feels tight, remind yourself of this verse and carry on doing good, even if no one thanks you.

en.title: Glorify Your Lord with Praise Before Sunrise
en.excerpt: Glorifying Allah at the ends of the day is a remedy for the heart against the hurtful words it hears from people.

body.text: Allah commands His Prophet ﷺ to be patient with what the deniers say, and guides him to glorify Him with praise before sunrise and before sunset, during hours of the night and at the ends of the day, concluding with a generous promise: «so that you may be content».
فَاصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ غُرُوبِهَا ۖ وَمِنْ آنَاءِ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْ وَأَطْرَافَ النَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرْضَىٰ

If your chest feels tight because of what people say, do not busy yourself with answering them; instead, occupy your tongue with glorification and praise in the morning, the evening and during the night. Remembrance fills the heart with tranquility, turns distress into contentment, and keeps your whole day surrounded by the remembrance of Allah from beginning to end.

en.title: Blessed Is He in Whose Hand Is the Dominion
en.excerpt: All dominion is in the hand of Allah alone; whoever attaches himself to Him fears nothing.

body.text: Surah Al-Mulk begins by extolling Allah: exalted is He and abundant is His goodness. In His hand alone is the dominion, which He disposes as He wills, and He has power over all things; nothing is beyond Him.
تَبَٰرَكَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٌ

The phrase «in whose hand is the dominion» sums up the reality of the universe: all authority, management, giving and withholding are in His hand, glory be to Him. So if you fear someone's power or hope for his favour, remember that all dominion is in Allah's hand, and direct your fear and hope to Him first.

Opening the verse with «Blessed is He» is an invitation to see goodness and blessing in Allah's management of affairs: whatever happens in His dominion comes from a Lord of abundant goodness who has power over all things. So think well of Him, and seek blessing from Him in your time, your wealth and your family.

en.title: Like a Grain That Grows Seven Ears
en.excerpt: Charity does not decrease wealth; it is a seed that Allah multiplies many times over.

body.text: In this verse Allah strikes a tangible parable close to everyone's experience: a single grain sown in the earth produces seven ears, and in every ear are a hundred grains. That is what Allah does with what His servant spends in His cause.

مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنۢبَتَتۡ سَبۡعَ سَنَابِلَ فِي كُلِّ سُنۢبُلَةٖ مِّاْئَةُ حَبَّةٖۗ وَٱللَّهُ يُضَٰعِفُ لِمَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ

So do not belittle your charity even if it is small; the One who makes the grain grow in the darkness of the soil is able to make your small deed grow until it is great in His sight. The verse's ending, that Allah is «All-Encompassing, All-Knowing», brings reassurance: His giving never runs short, and His knowledge encompasses your intention and sincerity, so not even an atom's weight is lost with Him.

en.title: And Sever Your Ties of Kinship
en.excerpt: Severing family ties goes hand in hand with spreading corruption in the land, and maintaining them is a sign of a sound heart.

body.text: The verse warns of a state in which turning away from obedience to Allah comes together with spreading corruption in the land and severing ties of kinship, as though the breakdown of family and relatives were a natural consequence of hearts drifting away from their Lord.
فَهَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ إِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ أَنْ تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَتُقَطِّعُوا أَرْحَامَكُمْ

Maintaining family ties is not merely a visit at Eid; it is asking after them, checking on them, sharing in their joy and sorrow, and taking the first step towards reconciliation in a dispute, even if you are in the right. Review your list of relatives: whom have you not seen for a long time? With whom is there coldness between you? Start today with a message or a call, for a small step may revive a tie that was about to be cut.

en.title: My Lord, Prison Is Dearer to Me
en.excerpt: Yusuf preferred the confinement of prison over the freedom of sin, and asked his Lord to avert the plotting from him.

body.text: Yusuf (peace be upon him) is given a choice between falling into what he is being called to or entering prison. He chooses prison willingly, and raises his hands to his Lord, admitting his weakness and asking Him to turn away from him what was being plotted against him.
قَالَ رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا يَدْعُونَنِي إِلَيْهِ ۖ وَإِلَّا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّي كَيْدَهُنَّ أَصْبُ إِلَيْهِنَّ وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ

A believer may pay a worldly price to preserve his religion, so that hardship with obedience becomes dearer to him than comfort with sin. This honest weighing is the mark of a living heart. Despite the strength of his stance, he was not deluded about himself; rather, he said: «and if You do not avert their plot from me». Steadfastness is a gift from Allah, and however righteous a servant becomes, he remains in need of his Lord's protection at every moment.

en.title: If You Count Allah's Blessings, You Could Not Enumerate Them
en.excerpt: Allah's blessings are too many to count, and out of His mercy He does not cut them off from us despite our shortcomings in thanking Him.

body.text: The verse opens a wide door of reflection before man: were he to try to count Allah's blessings upon him, he could not enumerate them. It then ends by stating that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, so He forgives the shortcoming in thanking Him and does not withhold the blessings because of it.
وَإِنْ تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ

Try one day to write down the blessings you can remember: a breath that comes and goes, eyes that see, safety, food, loved ones. You will find the list never ends, and you will realise that what you complain about is little in the ocean of what you have been given. How many blessings we only notice once we lose them.

This awareness gives rise in the heart to modesty before Allah and love for Him, moves one to thank Him in word and deed, and extinguishes the fire of grumbling that blinds the servant to the good surrounding him. So begin your day by recalling one blessing and thanking Allah for it.

en.title: That Which Brings You Near to Us
en.excerpt: It is not wealth and children that bring you near to Allah, but faith and righteous deeds.

body.text: In this verse Allah establishes a measure that differs from the measures of many people: wealth and children do not bring their owner nearer to Allah in rank, except whoever believes and does righteous deeds; for them is a multiplied reward, and they will be secure in the lofty chambers.

وَمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُكُمْ بِالَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِنْدَنَا زُلْفَىٰ إِلَّا مَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَأُولَٰئِكَ لَهُمْ جَزَاءُ الضِّعْفِ بِمَا عَمِلُوا وَهُمْ فِي الْغُرُفَاتِ آمِنُونَ

A person may be deluded by how much he owns, or saddened by how little, and the verse rearranges the standards: nearness to Allah comes through faith and deeds, not through bank balances. If you have been given wealth, make it a path to righteous deeds, and if your wealth is little, do not think that it lowers your standing with your Lord. And how beautiful is the ending: security in the lofty chambers after the fear and anxiety of this world.

en.title: He Was True to His Promise
en.excerpt: Being true to one's promise is a trait with which Allah praised a noble prophet, so it is worthy of us to adopt it.

body.text: When Allah mentioned His prophet Ismail (peace be upon him) in His Book, among the first of his qualities He mentioned was that he was true to his promise, teaching us that this trait is no minor detail but a quality mentioned in praise of the noble prophets.
وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ صَادِقَ الْوَعْدِ وَكَانَ رَسُولًا نَبِيًّا

Better to make few promises that you keep than many that you do not fulfil, and do not promise except what you are able to do. If you promise your children or your family something, keep it, for they learn truthfulness from your actions before your words, and their trust in you is built from the promises you keep.

en.title: My Lord, I Have Wronged Myself, So Forgive Me
en.excerpt: Musa admitted his mistake at once and asked for forgiveness, and the answer came in the very same verse.

body.text: After Musa (peace be upon him) unintentionally caused the man's death, he did not justify himself or evade; he hastened to confess before his Lord and ask for forgiveness. Allah then tells us that He forgave him, and that He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي فَغَفَرَ لَهُ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ

The quickest path to forgiveness is honest confession without justification. So if you err, do not delay repentance or search for excuses; rather, say with a humbled heart «My Lord, I have wronged myself», seek pardon from your Forgiving, Merciful Lord, and then resolve to set right what follows.

en.title: Everything with Him Is in Due Measure
en.excerpt: Nothing in your life came about by chance; everything with Allah is in a measure that neither exceeds nor falls short.

body.text: The two verses tell us that Allah knows what every female carries and what the wombs lessen and increase, and that everything with Him is in due measure; He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Most Great, the Most Exalted.

اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنْثَىٰ وَمَا تَغِيضُ الْأَرْحَامُ وَمَا تَزْدَادُ ۖ وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِمِقْدَارٍ
عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ الْكَبِيرُ الْمُتَعَالِ

Believing that «everything with Him is in due measure» gives the heart tranquility: a delay in provision, a difficulty in some matter, or the shortness of a span of time is not chaos, but a decree from One who is All-Knowing and All-Wise. So strive earnestly, and then be content with what comes after your striving.

And when you remember that He is «the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed», you do not judge matters by their outward appearance alone. Perhaps a lack you see today is wisdom itself, and perhaps an increase you wish for holds no good for you. So ask Allah for good in what you choose, and be content with what He chooses for you, for He knows the outcome of matters better than you.

en.title: But If You Conceal It, That Is Better for You
en.excerpt: Charity given openly is good, but secret charity is closer to sincerity and better at protecting the needy.

body.text: This verse praises charity in both its forms: if its giver discloses it, that is good, and if he conceals it and gives it to the poor, that is better for him. It then promises those who give charity the removal of their misdeeds, and reminds them that Allah is fully aware of what they do.
إِن تُبۡدُواْ ٱلصَّدَقَٰتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَۖ وَإِن تُخۡفُوهَا وَتُؤۡتُوهَا ٱلۡفُقَرَآءَ فَهُوَ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡۚ وَيُكَفِّرُ عَنكُم مِّن سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمۡۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرٞ

Concealing charity protects your heart from the love of praise and protects the dignity of the poor from having their need known before people; it is an act of worship that takes care of both sides. So keep a hidden charity that no one knows of but Allah, even if small, and be reassured that Allah «is fully aware of what you do»; nothing of what you concealed escapes Him.

en.title: Let Not Your Wealth or Your Children Divert You
en.excerpt: Children are a blessing that helps one remember Allah, not a distraction that turns one away from Him.

body.text: Allah calls out to the believers, warning them against letting wealth and children divert them from His remembrance and from His obligations, and describes whoever is so diverted as being among the losers, because he has put what perishes before what endures.
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُلْهِكُمْ أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُكُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ ۚ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ

Loving one's children and working for their provision is worship when kept within its bounds, but it becomes a trial when it delays prayer or extinguishes remembrance in the heart. The solution is to make our families our partners in obedience: praying together at home, remembrance on the road, supplication before sleep. Then children become a reason for remembrance instead of a cause of heedlessness.

en.title: I Only Complain of My Grief and Sorrow to Allah
en.excerpt: Yaqub pours out his grief to his Lord alone, and urges his sons never to despair of Allah's mercy.

body.text: Yaqub's (peace be upon him) separation from his two sons lasted so long that his eyes turned white with grief. Yet his grief did not turn into despair; he directed his complaint to Allah, and then commanded his sons to go out and search, full of hope.

قَالَ إِنَّمَا أَشْكُو بَثِّي وَحُزْنِي إِلَى اللَّهِ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
يَا بَنِيَّ اذْهَبُوا فَتَحَسَّسُوا مِنْ يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَيْأَسُوا مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهُ لَا يَيْأَسُ مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْكَافِرُونَ

Weeping and sorrow do not contradict patience, so long as the complaint is made to Allah and not about Him. If your chest feels tight, make your intimate prayer to your Lord, for He knows your state best and is most able to remove what afflicts you. Yaqub did not stop at supplication; he said: «Go and search diligently». True hope drives one to act and take the means, and despairing of Allah's mercy is not among the traits of believers, however long the trial lasts.

en.title: We Will Surely Grant Him a Good Life
en.excerpt: Righteous deeds joined with faith bear the fruit of a good life in this world and the best reward in the Hereafter.

body.text: A generous promise that includes men and women alike: whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer, Allah will grant him a good life, then reward him according to the best of what he used to do. How generous a promise it is for everyone who strives in goodness!
مَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحًا مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً ۖ وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ

A good life does not mean a life free of hardships; it is a life filled with contentment, satisfaction, tranquility and success in doing good, so that its owner finds spaciousness in his heart even when some circumstances become tight. Goodness in life is the fruit of the heart before it is the fruit of circumstances.

So if you want a good life, do not look for it in abundant wealth alone, but in faith and righteous deeds, for they are the key to serenity in this world. And in His words «according to the best of what they used to do» is glad tidings of a bounty that exceeds the deed. So do much good, even if it is little.

en.title: Whoever Desires the Harvest of the Hereafter
en.excerpt: Whoever sows for the Hereafter, Allah increases his harvest; whoever sows for this world alone finds nothing else.

body.text: Allah likens deeds to tilling and sowing: whoever seeks the reward of the Hereafter through his deeds, Allah increases his harvest and multiplies it for him; and whoever makes this world his sole aim, Allah gives him from it what has been apportioned to him, and he has no share in the Hereafter.
مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الْآخِرَةِ نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ ۖ وَمَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الدُّنْيَا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا وَمَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ نَصِيبٍ

Every one of your days is a field in which you sow, and the question is: for which harvest are you sowing? A single deed may be a harvest for this world or for the Hereafter depending on the intention. The worker earning his living and the student at his studies, if they intend thereby the pleasure of Allah, their work becomes sowing for the Hereafter, and they still do not miss their apportioned share of this world.

en.title: Close Friends on That Day
en.excerpt: Only companionship founded on God-consciousness remains a friendship on the Day of Resurrection.

body.text: The verse reveals the fate of friendships on the Day of Resurrection: every close friendship built on something other than obedience to Allah turns into enmity, except the companionship of the God-conscious, which was brought together by faith and cooperation in goodness; that remains and grows.
الْأَخِلَّاءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ إِلَّا الْمُتَّقِينَ

So look at your companions: do your friends help you with prayer, truthfulness and good character, or do they drag you towards what you will regret? Choose a friend who reminds you of Allah when you are heedless and gives you sincere advice when you err, and be that for others too. True friendship is an investment whose effect extends from this world to the Hereafter.

en.title: My Lord, I Am in Need of Whatever Good You Send Down to Me
en.excerpt: The supplication of a weary stranger who did good to others and then showed his need before his Lord.

body.text: Musa (peace be upon him) arrived in Madyan a stranger, afraid and exhausted. He watered the flock for the two women without waiting for any reward, then withdrew to the shade and showed his Lord his need and his poverty for any good He might send his way.
فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰ إِلَى الظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَا أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ

When you do good to people, do not wait for a reward from them; turn with your need to Allah. This supplication holds a beautiful etiquette: Musa did not specify a particular request, but showed his dependence and accepted whatever good Allah would choose for him. After that came relief, shelter and marriage.

en.title: Say: Allah Is the Creator of All Things
en.excerpt: Since He alone is the Creator, He alone deserves to be hoped in, feared and worshipped.

body.text: The verse begins with a question about the Lord of the heavens and the earth and answers that it is Allah. It then condemns taking as protectors those who have no power to benefit or harm even themselves, and concludes that Allah is the Creator of all things and He is the One, the Prevailing.

قُلْ مَنْ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ قُلِ اللَّهُ ۚ قُلْ أَفَاتَّخَذْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ نَفْعًا وَلَا ضَرًّا ۚ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الْأَعْمَىٰ وَالْبَصِيرُ أَمْ هَلْ تَسْتَوِي الظُّلُمَاتُ وَالنُّورُ ۗ أَمْ جَعَلُوا لِلَّهِ شُرَكَاءَ خَلَقُوا كَخَلْقِهِ فَتَشَابَهَ الْخَلْقُ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ قُلِ اللَّهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ

Among the clearest proofs of Allah's oneness is this question: who has the power to benefit or harm himself? If a created being cannot even benefit himself, how can the heart be attached to him? So review where you place your hope and fear, and direct them to the One who is «the One, the Prevailing».

In the contrast between «the blind and the seeing» and «darkness and light» there is a hint that affirming Allah's oneness is insight and light, while attachment to other than Allah is blindness and darkness. So ask Allah to make the light of faith firm in your heart, and make it part of your supplication that He shows you the truth as truth and grants you to follow it, for insight is a blessing to be asked for.

en.title: That They May Witness Benefits for Themselves
en.excerpt: Hajj is a season that gathers the benefits of religion and of this world, the greatest of which is the remembrance of Allah.

body.text: This verse explains some of the wisdom behind Hajj: that people may witness benefits for themselves, mention the name of Allah on known days, and feed the miserable and poor. It is an act of worship that brings together the heart, the body and wealth.
لِيَشْهَدُوا مَنَافِعَ لَهُمْ وَيَذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ فِي أَيَّامٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ عَلَىٰ مَا رَزَقَهُمْ مِنْ بَهِيمَةِ الْأَنْعَامِ ۖ فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا الْبَائِسَ الْفَقِيرَ

The benefits here are broad: forgiveness and mercy, Muslims from every place getting to know one another, training the soul in patience and humility, and a reminder that people are equal before their Lord. Whoever is not able to perform Hajj, let him take his share of its spirit: remembering Allah abundantly in the virtuous days, feeding the needy, and keeping in mind that the goal of every act of worship is that Allah be remembered and thanked for His blessings.

en.title: My Lord, Forgive Me and My Parents
en.excerpt: A single supplication that embraces oneself, one's parents, one's household and all the believers.

body.text: At the close of his call, Nuh (peace be upon him) asked his Lord for forgiveness for himself, then for his parents, then for whoever entered his house as a believer, then for the believing men and women. The circle of his supplication widened from the closest to the farthest.
رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِمَنْ دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًا

This is how the believer's heart should be: he does not forget his parents in his supplication, nor neglect his household, and then his heart expands to include his brothers and sisters everywhere. Make this supplication a regular part of your remembrance and teach it to your children, for it plants in them, all at once, kindness to parents, love for their household, and a sense of belonging to the community of believers.

en.title: And upon Him Let Those Who Rely Put Their Trust
en.excerpt: Yaqub advised his sons to be cautious and take precautions, then returned the whole matter to Allah.

body.text: Yaqub (peace be upon him) bids farewell to his sons as they head to Egypt, advising them to enter through separate gates rather than a single one. He then explains to them that this plan cannot avail them anything against Allah's decree, and that reliance is upon Him alone.

وَقَالَ يَا بَنِيَّ لَا تَدْخُلُوا مِنْ بَابٍ وَاحِدٍ وَادْخُلُوا مِنْ أَبْوَابٍ مُتَفَرِّقَةٍ ۖ وَمَا أُغْنِي عَنْكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ۖ إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ ۖ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ ۖ وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ

This advice holds a beautiful balance between taking the means and relying on Allah. Yaqub (peace be upon him) did not abandon caution on the pretext of fate, nor did he rely on caution alone; he combined wise planning with faith that «the decision rests only with Allah».

So should the believer be in his travel, his work, his health and his wealth: he takes precautions, plans and seeks counsel, then surrenders his heart to Allah. He is not deluded by his means when he succeeds, nor does he despair when the results do not come as he wished.

en.title: We Made the Night and the Day Two Signs
en.excerpt: The alternation of night and day is a sign pointing to Allah, and a blessing by which people's lives are ordered.

body.text: Night and day repeat before our eyes every day until we almost stop noticing them, and the Qur'an draws our attention to the fact that they are two signs: night for rest, and a bright day for seeking provision, and by their alternation the number of years and the reckoning of time are known.

وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ آيَتَيْنِ ۖ فَمَحَوْنَا آيَةَ اللَّيْلِ وَجَعَلْنَا آيَةَ النَّهَارِ مُبْصِرَةً لِتَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَلِتَعْلَمُوا عَدَدَ السِّنِينَ وَالْحِسَابَ ۚ وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ فَصَّلْنَاهُ تَفْصِيلًا

Time itself is a sign and a blessing, and every day that passes is a page of one's life folded away. Whoever reflects on this verse realises that every time has its function: the rest of the night helps with the work of the day, and the work of the day is a seeking of Allah's bounty.

So order your day by this balance, and do not turn night into day and day into night without need. At every sunset and sunrise, recall that Allah has explained everything in detail, and nothing in the universe is without purpose.

en.title: What Is with Allah Is Better and More Lasting
en.excerpt: Everything you have been given is temporary enjoyment, and what is with Allah is better in itself and more enduring.

body.text: The verse reminds us of the reality of everything in our hands: it is the enjoyment of the life of this world, enjoyed for a little while and then gone, while what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who combine two noble qualities: faith, and reliance on their Lord in all their affairs.
فَمَا أُوتِيتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَمَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَىٰ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ

When an opportunity passes you by or something you love is taken from you, remember that it was mere enjoyment, and that what is with Allah has not escaped you. Reflect on how the verse links this lasting good with reliance on Allah: whoever's heart is at peace with his Lord finds what he missed of this world easy to bear, and does not chase after it breathlessly for fear of missing out.

en.title: Woe to Those Who Give Short Measure
en.excerpt: Whoever demands his right in full should give others their right in full.

body.text: The surah opens with a severe warning to those who take their due from people in full, but when they measure or weigh for them, they give less. The flaw is not in the transaction alone, but in the scale of the soul that demands for itself what it does not give to others.

وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ
الَّذِينَ إِذَا اكْتَالُوا عَلَى النَّاسِ يَسْتَوْفُونَ
وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ

Giving short measure takes many forms: demanding excellence from people while not being excellent yourself, holding them to account for shortcomings while excusing yourself, wanting their respect while not respecting them. So measure how you treat people by how you would like them to treat you, and keep a single scale for yourself and against yourself.

en.title: Our Lord, Do Not Make Us a Trial for the Disbelievers
en.excerpt: The believer asks his Lord that his conduct not become a reason for turning people away from the truth.

body.text: This is part of the supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and those with him, whom Allah made an excellent example for the believers. They ask their Lord not to make them a trial for those who disbelieve and to forgive them their sins, calling upon Him by His names the Almighty, the All-Wise.
رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا رَبَّنَا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ

A Muslim's conduct is a message that people read before they hear his words. If they see weakness or bad character, they may think the fault lies in the religion itself. So ask Allah to protect you from becoming an argument against the truth, and strive to let people see in your character and dealings a true picture of what you believe.

en.title: Had There Been Gods in Them Besides Allah, They Would Have Been Ruined
en.excerpt: The order of the whole universe is a silent witness that its Disposer is One with no partner.

body.text: A clear rational proof mentioned by the Qur'an: had there been multiple deities in the heavens and the earth besides Allah, they would have been ruined by their rivalry, yet what we witness is order and precision. It is followed by declaring Allah, Lord of the Throne, far above what the polytheists ascribe to Him.
لَوۡ كَانَ فِيهِمَآ ءَالِهَةٌ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَاۚ فَسُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَرۡشِ عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ

Whenever you see the sun rise on time, the seasons follow one another, and the precision of your own creation, remember this verse: a single order points to a single Disposer. Let your contemplation of the universe be an act of worship that increases your certainty, not merely a passing glance.

Among the fruits of this certainty is that your heart becomes unified just as the universe is unified: it is no longer torn between hope in this one and fear of that one, but gathers upon one Lord whom it hopes in, fears and loves. When the heart is gathered upon its Lord, it is relieved of distraction, all its striving goes in one direction, and so the soul is calmed and its affairs set straight.

en.title: But What Reaches Him Is the Piety from You
en.excerpt: The value of worship lies not in its outward form, but in the God-consciousness that dwells in the heart.

body.text: The verse speaks of the sacrificial animals of Hajj and Eid, stating that none of their flesh or blood reaches Allah; what reaches Him is the piety, sincerity and reverence in the heart of the one who offers them.
لَنْ يَنَالَ اللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَاؤُهَا وَلَٰكِنْ يَنَالُهُ التَّقْوَىٰ مِنْكُمْ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمْ لِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَاكُمْ ۗ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُحْسِنِينَ

This is a principle in every act of worship: prayer, charity and fasting have an outward form and an inner spirit, which is God-consciousness, and Allah looks at the spirit before the form. Before you perform any act of worship, ask yourself: for whom am I doing this, and what is in my heart right now? Correcting the intention makes a small deed great, and its absence turns a great deed into scattered dust.

en.title: They Enjoin One Another to Truth and to Patience
en.excerpt: Salvation is not a solo project; believers counsel one another and strengthen each other.

body.text: The verse exempts from loss those who combine faith and righteous deeds, and add to them counselling one another to the truth and to patience in upholding it. An individual's righteousness is not complete in isolation from the righteousness of those around him.
إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْا بِالصَّبْرِ

The Muslim home is the first arena for this mutual counsel: a spouse who reminds the other of good, a brother who encourages his brother, and parents who are patient with their children and help them to be patient. The wording implies participation from both sides, so be one who accepts advice just as you offer it, and offer it gently and at the right time, so that it is a help and not a burden.

en.title: Our Lord, Accept This from Us
en.excerpt: They build the greatest House and then ask for acceptance; the believer works and fears that his deed may not be accepted.

body.text: Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them) raise the foundations of the Sacred House, among the noblest of deeds, and yet you find in their words no pride in what they did, only a humble supplication that Allah accept it from them.
وَإِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلۡ مِنَّآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ

What counts is not the amount of deeds alone, but their acceptance by Allah. That is why one of the qualities of the righteous is that they strive in obedience and then ask their Lord for acceptance, without being deluded by what they have offered. Make this supplication the seal of your deeds: your prayer, your charity, your teaching and your service to people. And remember that Allah is «the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing»; He hears your supplication and knows your intention, so set your intention right and your deed will be set right.

en.title: That Which Is Healing and Mercy for the Believers
en.excerpt: The Qur'an is a cure for hearts from doubt and anxiety, and a mercy for whoever believes in it and acts upon it.

body.text: Allah describes His Book as healing and mercy for the believers: it cures hearts of doubts, ignorance and sorrows and pours mercy and tranquility upon them, while it only increases those who turn away from it in loss.
وَنُنَزِّلُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ مَا هُوَ شِفَاءٌ وَرَحْمَةٌ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ۙ وَلَا يَزِيدُ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا خَسَارًا

Healing requires the patient to take the medicine. Whoever wants the Qur'an to have its effect on his heart must turn to it with recitation, reflection and action, not merely keep it on shelves for blessing. The Qur'an bears its fruit for whoever opens his heart to it and comes to it with sincerity and need.

If a worry or confusion weighs you down, open the Mushaf with the intention of seeking healing, read slowly and pause at the meanings, and you will find that the verses touch the place of pain and bind it with Allah's mercy. Make that your habit in every difficulty, not only in times of great hardship.

en.title: He Accepts Repentance from His Servants
en.excerpt: The door of repentance is open; Allah accepts it from His servants, pardons their misdeeds and knows their sincerity.

body.text: A verse that opens the door of hope for hearts: it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants, pardons misdeeds and knows what they do. Neither the sincerity of the one who repents, nor the brokenness of his heart, nor his regret over the past is hidden from Him.
وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَعْفُو عَنِ السَّيِّئَاتِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ

Satan may stand between the servant and his repentance, saying: your sins are too great to be forgiven, or: you will go back to them, so there is no point. The verse refutes all of that: Allah accepts repentance and pardons, and He knows your weakness. So turn to Him now with sincere regret and a resolve to reform, and do not delay, for the One awaiting you is a Lord who accepts and pardons.

en.title: That Is the One Who Repulses the Orphan
en.excerpt: Harshness towards the orphan and neglect of the poor are among the effects of weak faith in the Recompense.

body.text: The surah links denying the Day of Recompense with two ugly traits: harshly pushing away the orphan, and failing to encourage the feeding of the poor. Faith in the Recompense is not merely an idea in the mind; it is mercy that shows itself in how the weak are treated.

أَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى يُكَذِّبُ بِٱلدِّينِ
فَذَٰلِكَ ٱلَّذِى يَدُعُّ ٱلْيَتِيمَ
وَلَا يَحُضُّ عَلَىٰ طَعَامِ ٱلْمِسْكِينِ

So when you see an orphan, honour him with a word or a tender touch. And do not be content with feeding the poor yourself; remind others and urge them to do the same, for the verse censured even the failure to encourage it. The more your heart softens towards the weak, the more it shows that your faith in meeting Allah is alive.

en.title: Glorify Your Lord with Praise When You Arise
en.excerpt: Patience with Allah's decree brings reassurance: you are under your Lord's watchful eyes, so glorify Him when you rise and through the night.

body.text: Allah reassures His Prophet ﷺ that he is under His care and protection, «for indeed you are in Our eyes», commands him to be patient with His decree, and then guides him to glorify Him when he arises, during part of the night, and at the setting of the stars just before dawn.

وَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا ۖ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَإِدْبَارَ النُّجُومِ

Among the greatest aids to patience is keeping in mind that Allah sees you and protects you. Then tie your day to glorification: when you rise from sleep or from a gathering, in the hours of the night, and as dawn approaches. These are brief moments that bring the heart back to its Lord and fill it with serenity.

en.title: We Made from Water Every Living Thing
en.excerpt: In every drop of water you drink is a sign calling you to faith and gratitude.

body.text: The verse draws attention to two great signs: the heavens and the earth were joined together and Allah parted them, and He made from water every living thing. It then asks a question that stirs the heart: will they not then believe?
أَوَلَمۡ يَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ كَانَتَا رَتۡقٗا فَفَتَقۡنَٰهُمَاۖ وَجَعَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَآءِ كُلَّ شَيۡءٍ حَيٍّۚ أَفَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ

Water is the closest thing to you and the most frequent in your day, yet Allah made it the origin of every living being. So let your drinking and your ablution be moments of remembrance, and say to yourself: this is from the bounty of my Lord, who made life from water.

The verse's ending, «will they not then believe?», draws attention to the fact that signs are never lacking; what is lacking is reflection. So set aside a few minutes each day to reflect on a familiar blessing, for faith increases through reflection. Begin with water itself: consider how it comes down, flows and revives the earth, then praise Allah for it.

en.title: That Is from the Piety of Hearts
en.excerpt: Honouring the symbols of Allah is a sign of a living heart that knows the greatness of its Lord.

body.text: This short verse links an outward deed, honouring the symbols of Allah, with an inner root, the piety of hearts. Whoever honours what Allah has honoured shows the reverence that has settled in his heart.
ذَٰلِكَ وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّهَا مِنْ تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ

Among the ways of honouring these symbols: approaching the prayer with calm, respecting the mosque and the Mushaf, and welcoming the virtuous days with preparation and joy rather than listlessness. If you find in yourself a disregard for any of the symbols of the religion, know that the heart needs watering; so reflect much on the names and attributes of Allah, and everything associated with Him will grow great in your eyes.

en.title: And Lower Your Wing to the Believers
en.excerpt: Humility and gentleness towards the believers are among the most beautiful forms of brotherhood.

body.text: The verse directs the Prophet ﷺ not to extend his eyes towards the fleeting enjoyment of this world that others have been given, nor to grieve over them, and then commands him to lower his wing to the believers, that is, to be humble and gentle with them.
لَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ إِلَىٰ مَا مَتَّعْنَا بِهِ أَزْوَاجًا مِنْهُمْ وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَاخْفِضْ جَنَاحَكَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ

Lowering the wing is the image of a bird drawing its young close to itself, full of tenderness, mercy and protection. So should the believer be with his brothers and his family: close, easy-going, neither haughty nor affected. Combining the abandonment of longing for what others have with humility towards the believers hints that a heart preoccupied with comparison finds it hard to soften towards its brothers.

en.title: In a Valley Without Cultivation
en.excerpt: Ibrahim left his family in a barren valley out of trust in Allah, and made his aim that they establish prayer.

body.text: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) stands in a valley with no cultivation, where he has settled some of his offspring near the Sacred House. He calls upon his Lord with the heart of a caring father and a trusting believer, and explains the purpose of it all.

رَبَّنَا إِنِّي أَسْكَنْتُ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي بِوَادٍ غَيْرِ ذِي زَرْعٍ عِنْدَ بَيْتِكَ الْمُحَرَّمِ رَبَّنَا لِيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ وَارْزُقْهُمْ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ

Notice the order of priorities in the supplication: he first mentioned «that they may establish prayer», then asked that people's hearts incline towards them and that they be given provision. The righteous father cares about his children's religion before their worldly life, without neglecting their needs. He ended his supplication with «so that they may be grateful», for provision is a blessing that calls for gratitude. This is how the believer raises his family: to see blessings as a means to obeying Allah, not as an end in themselves.

en.title: Have You Not Seen How Your Lord Extends the Shadow?
en.excerpt: In the calm daily movement of the shadow is a sign of Allah's precise management of this universe.

body.text: The verse invites us to look at a familiar scene: the shadow stretched across the ground, the sun that serves as its guide so that it lengthens and shortens, and then Allah draws it in little by little, «a gradual withdrawal». Had He willed, He could have made it stationary.

أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيۡفَ مَدَّ ٱلظِّلَّ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ لَجَعَلَهُۥ سَاكِنٗا ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَا ٱلشَّمۡسَ عَلَيۡهِ دَلِيلٗا
ثُمَّ قَبَضۡنَٰهُ إِلَيۡنَا قَبۡضٗا يَسِيرٗا

The greatest signs may lie in the simplest things we see every day, but familiarity extinguishes wonder. The believer revives his gaze, and sees in shadow and light and in their gentle gradualness the kindness and wisdom of Allah. So reflect on the shadow once as you walk, and remember the One who extended it.

In the gradualness of «a gradual withdrawal» there is a lesson in Allah's ways: change in the universe and in souls usually comes little by little. So do not be impatient for the fruit of reforming yourself, and persevere with small, successive steps, for every sincere step brings you closer to your goal.

en.title: Closer to Him Than His Jugular Vein
en.excerpt: Allah knows what your soul whispers to you; so be mindful of Him in your thoughts before your actions.

body.text: The verse affirms that Allah created man and knows what his soul whispers to him, and that He is closer to him, through His knowledge and encompassment, than his jugular vein. No passing thought or whisper of the soul escapes His knowledge, let alone a word or a deed.
وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ ۖ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ

This closeness instils two things in the believer's heart: an awe that keeps him from sin in private, and an intimacy that comforts him when he feels alone. If you are about to do something wrong, remember that your Lord knows what is in your soul; and if your chest feels tight, know that He is closer to you than anyone, and knows your complaint before you voice it.

en.title: Render Trusts to Those Entitled to Them
en.excerpt: Trustworthiness and justice are two foundations upon which people's well-being rests in every setting.

body.text: The verse commands two great matters: rendering trusts to those they belong to, and judging between people with justice. It then describes this as an excellent thing with which Allah admonishes us. They are among the most comprehensive of morals, by which the family, the workplace and society are set right.

إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهَا وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ أَنْ تَحْكُمُوا بِالْعَدْلِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا

A trust is broader than financial deposits: time at work is a trust, a secret is a trust, and the responsibility you have been given is a trust. Justice is not for judges alone; you judge between your children, between your colleagues, and in your opinions about people. So render every trust to those entitled to it, and be just even towards those you do not love, for Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

en.title: He Will Find Allah Forgiving and Merciful
en.excerpt: The door of seeking forgiveness is open to everyone who has done wrong or wronged himself, and the promise in it is explicit.

body.text: This verse opens the door of hope for every sinner: whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then returns to Allah seeking forgiveness will find Allah forgiving of his sin and merciful to him, whatever his sin may be.
وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ سُوءًا أَوْ يَظْلِمْ نَفْسَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ يَجِدِ اللَّهَ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا

Do not let sin become a barrier between you and your Lord, for the verse promises the one who seeks forgiveness that he will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful. Whenever your foot slips, return quickly, and make seeking forgiveness an unbroken daily habit, for it erases the effect of sin and restores the heart's clarity.

en.title: Do People Think They Will Be Left Alone?
en.excerpt: Faith is not just a word that is spoken; it is sincerity that shows itself when tested.

body.text: Surah Al-Ankabut opens with a question that awakens the heart: do people think they will be left to say «We believe» without being tested? It then reminds us that Allah tested those before them, so that the truthful in faith would be distinguished from the liar.

أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتۡرَكُوٓاْ أَن يَقُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفۡتَنُونَ
وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۖ فَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ

If a trial befalls you, do not interpret it as Allah abandoning you; the verse establishes that testing is a constant law for everyone who says «We believe». Rather, see it as an opportunity for your sincerity to become evident, and hold fast to patience and righteous deeds.

Another benefit is that knowing this law lightens the impact of calamity, for what is expected is easier than what comes as a surprise. Whoever knows the path contains tests prepares for them with supplication, remembrance and the company of the righteous, and asks Allah for steadfastness before the trial arrives.

en.title: Bow, Prostrate and Do Good
en.excerpt: The path to success combines prayer that connects the servant to his Lord with goodness that connects him to people.

body.text: This noble call contains a beautiful progression: bowing and prostrating, then worshipping Allah in general, then doing good; all of it a single path that ends in the hope of success. Let us reflect on how this call brings together worship and kindness to others.
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ارْكَعُوا وَاسْجُدُوا وَاعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ وَافْعَلُوا الْخَيْرَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ

So do not confine your worship to the mosque, nor separate your good deeds from your prayer. Prostration softens the heart, and a soft heart is moved to do good to creation. Set yourself a good deed every day after your prayer, even a small one: a kind word, help for a relative, or a hidden charity; perhaps Allah will write success for you through it.

en.title: That He Might Find Tranquility in Her
en.excerpt: The purpose of marriage is a refuge in which the soul finds rest, not an arena of constant conflict.

body.text: The verse recalls the single origin of creation, and that Allah made from the soul its mate so that he might find tranquility in her. It then describes the couple calling upon their Lord together when the pregnancy grew heavy, hoping for a righteous child and promising to be grateful.

۞ هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍۢ وَٰحِدَةٍۢ وَجَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا لِيَسْكُنَ إِلَيْهَا ۖ فَلَمَّا تَغَشَّىٰهَا حَمَلَتْ حَمْلًا خَفِيفًۭا فَمَرَّتْ بِهِۦ ۖ فَلَمَّآ أَثْقَلَت دَّعَوَا ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُمَا لَئِنْ ءَاتَيْتَنَا صَٰلِحًۭا لَّنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ

A home founded on tranquility is one in which each spouse finds rest and security, returning to it from the toil of life as a traveller returns to his shelter. One of the most beautiful things in the verse is the image of the couple calling upon Allah together; so give your home moments of shared supplication, especially when awaiting a blessing or facing a worry, and fulfil your gratitude when the blessing comes.

en.title: And He Brought a Fat Calf
en.excerpt: Ibrahim honours guests he does not know, hastening to bring food and offering it to them kindly.

body.text: Strangers come in to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and greet him with peace. He returns the greeting, then goes quietly to his family and comes back with a fat calf, places it near them himself, and offers them the food with a gentle word.

إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ فَقَالُواْ سَلَٰمٗاۖ قَالَ سَلَٰمٞ قَوۡمٞ مُّنكَرُونَ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجۡلٖ سَمِينٖ
فَقَرَّبَهُۥٓ إِلَيۡهِمۡ قَالَ أَلَا تَأۡكُلُونَ

These verses give a complete picture of honouring a guest: returning the greeting, hastening to offer hospitality without the guest asking, presenting the best of what one has, bringing the food close to him, and then inviting him gently without insistence. Ibrahim honoured his guests before he knew who they were; generosity for him was a constant trait that did not depend on the guest's standing. So let us revive this trait in our homes, and receive our guests with cheerfulness and generosity.

en.title: Rely on Allah, and Allah Suffices as a Guardian
en.excerpt: Whoever makes Allah his Guardian, He suffices him, and he need not carry the burden of his affairs alone.

body.text: A short and comprehensive command: that the servant rely on Allah in all his affairs, followed by the reassurance that Allah suffices whoever relies on Him, protecting him and taking care of his affairs. These are words that serve as provision for the heart every day.
وَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ وَكِيلٗا

True reliance does not mean abandoning action; it means exerting your effort while your heart is attached to Allah, not to the means. When that is achieved, the soul is relieved of the weight of anxiety, because it knows its affair is in the hand of a Guardian whom nothing can defeat.
