Before every task you undertake, renew this meaning in your heart and say to yourself: it is enough for me that Allah is my Guardian. Then proceed with confidence and calm, and be content with what He chooses for you. Whoever has Allah as his Guardian is never lost.

en.title: And the Stupor of Death Comes in Truth
en.excerpt: Death is a reality man avoids for a long time, and then it comes to him without appointment.

body.text: The verse describes a moment no one can escape: the stupor of death arriving in truth. It then addresses man, saying: that is «what you used to avoid», meaning that what you were fleeing from and avoiding mention of has now come to you.
وَجَاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ ۖ ذَٰلِكَ مَا كُنْتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ

Many people avoid death, not by fleeing from it, for that is impossible, but by being heedless of it and postponing preparation for it. Remembering death is not a call to despair, but to setting the present right: to repent today, return rights to their owners, and reconnect with those you cut off, so that when that moment comes it finds you prepared rather than fleeing.

en.title: Respond with a Better Greeting
en.excerpt: Returning a greeting with a better one is a trait that sows affection among people.

body.text: The verse guides us to a beautiful daily courtesy: if someone greets you, respond with a greeting better than theirs, or at least its equal. It ends by stating that Allah takes account of all things; even a kind word of greeting is counted with Allah.
وَإِذَا حُيِّيتُمْ بِتَحِيَّةٍ فَحَيُّوا بِأَحْسَنَ مِنْهَا أَوْ رُدُّوهَا ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَسِيبًا

So make your reply to a greeting fuller and warmer: add to the words, turn your face towards the person, and smile. Do not underestimate this small courtesy, for it opens hearts, melts coldness and makes meeting you a pleasure for people. And if others fall short in greeting, do not fall short yourself.

en.title: Our Lord, Accept This from Us
en.excerpt: Ibrahim and Ismail build the House of Allah and then ask for acceptance, without being deluded by their deed.

body.text: While Ibrahim and Ismail (peace be upon them) were raising the foundations of the Sacred House, they were supplicating Allah to accept it from them, to make them submissive to Him, to make from their descendants a nation submissive to Him, to show them their rites, and to accept their repentance.

وَإِذۡ يَرۡفَعُ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ ٱلۡقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلۡ مِنَّآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
رَبَّنَا وَٱجۡعَلۡنَا مُسۡلِمَيۡنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَآ أُمَّةٗ مُّسۡلِمَةٗ لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبۡ عَلَيۡنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

However great your deed, do not be impressed with it; ask Allah to accept it, for what matters is not the amount of the deed but its acceptance. Carry concern for your descendants in your supplication as the two friends of Allah did, and conclude every act of obedience by asking for repentance, for the servant needs it in every state.

en.title: Allah Provides for It and for You
en.excerpt: How many creatures neither carry nor store their provision, yet Allah provides for them every day; so do not worry.

body.text: The verse draws attention to many creatures that are unable to gather or carry their provision, yet Allah provides for them just as He provides for people. It ends by stating that He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from whom nothing of His creatures' conditions is hidden.
وَكَأَيِّن مِّن دَآبَّةٖ لَّا تَحۡمِلُ رِزۡقَهَا ٱللَّهُ يَرۡزُقُهَا وَإِيَّاكُمۡۚ وَهُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ

Consider the birds and insects around you: they have no storehouses or accounts, and yet they rarely go to sleep hungry. So if your chest feels tight with worry over provision, remember «Allah provides for it and for you», and seek it through lawful means without panic or despair.

Linking provision with the names «the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing» reassures you that your supplication is heard and your need is known. So do not let fear of poverty drive you to what is unlawful or to abandoning good, for the Provider is One whose treasuries never run out. Seek your provision with a tranquil soul and a heart confident that what has been written for you will reach you.

en.title: When the Prayer Is Concluded, Disperse
en.excerpt: Islam connects the mosque to the marketplace, and worship to the pursuit of provision.

body.text: After the command to hasten to the Friday prayer, this verse comes to permit dispersing through the land and seeking the bounty of Allah. There is no monasticism that halts life, nor preoccupation with the world that makes one forget the prayer.
فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةُ فَٱنتَشِرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرًۭا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ

What is beautiful is that the verse does not cut off remembrance after leaving the mosque; rather, it says «and remember Allah much». The believer carries the remembrance of his Lord into his work, his trade and his journey. So make your daily work an extension of your prayer: honesty in dealings, truthfulness in speech, and a tongue kept moist with remembrance. In this way, seeking provision becomes an act of worship through which success is hoped for.

en.title: The Near Neighbour and the Distant Neighbour
en.excerpt: The circle of kindness begins with parents and widens until it includes the near and the distant neighbour.

body.text: After the command to worship Allah alone, the verse lists those who deserve kindness: parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbour, the distant neighbour, the companion at one's side and the wayfarer. It then censures the arrogant and boastful.

وَاعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئًا ۖ وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَبِذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَالْجَارِ ذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْجَارِ الْجُنُبِ وَالصَّاحِبِ بِالْجَنْبِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَنْ كَانَ مُخْتَالًا فَخُورًا

The neighbour in this verse is of two kinds: one who is near by kinship or residence, and one who is distant with no kinship between you; each has the right to kindness. Begin with the greeting of peace, check on how they are, and share whatever food or help you can. The verse's closing censure of the arrogant and boastful draws attention to the fact that pride is the greatest obstacle to kindness, for the arrogant person does not see the rights people have over him.

en.title: O My Father
en.excerpt: Ibrahim called his father to the truth with the gentlest words, repeating the call of kindness and mercy.

body.text: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) addresses his father, who worships idols. He is neither harsh with him nor contemptuous, but calls him time after time with words of love, explaining the truth to him with calm argument and sincere compassion.

إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَا أَبَتِ لِمَ تَعْبُدُ مَا لَا يَسْمَعُ وَلَا يُبْصِرُ وَلَا يُغْنِي عَنْكَ شَيْئًا
يَا أَبَتِ إِنِّي قَدْ جَاءَنِي مِنَ الْعِلْمِ مَا لَمْ يَأْتِكَ فَاتَّبِعْنِي أَهْدِكَ صِرَاطًا سَوِيًّا
يَا أَبَتِ لَا تَعْبُدِ الشَّيْطَانَ ۖ إِنَّ الشَّيْطَانَ كَانَ لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَصِيًّا

The truth does not need harsh wording; it needs sincerity and gentleness. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) combined in his call clear argument with refined manners: he began with a question, then explained the knowledge he had, then warned him against obeying Satan. This is a method for anyone who calls a family member to good: to preserve the right of kinship and respect, and to show compassion rather than superiority, for a merciful word is closer to hearts.

en.title: And I Entrust My Affair to Allah
en.excerpt: After giving advice and doing one's duty, the heart finds its rest in entrusting the matter to Allah.

body.text: These words come at the close of sincere advice offered by a believing man to his people, who turned away from him. He did not argue and did not despair; rather, he said: «And I entrust my affair to Allah», certain that Allah sees His servants.
فَسَتَذْكُرُونَ مَا أَقُولُ لَكُمْ ۚ وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِي إِلَى اللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ

This is a great psychological method: to do your part in speaking the truth and giving advice, and then not carry the burden of outcomes that are not in your hands, for people's hearts and decisions are not yours to own. This protects your heart from both regret and anger.

If you advise a relative or friend and they do not respond, do not burn with regret or cut off affection; rather, entrust their affair and yours to Allah, for He sees and knows, and sincerity of intention is never lost with Him. And keep praying for them in their absence.

en.title: And Came with a Heart Turning in Repentance
en.excerpt: Paradise is brought near to whoever feared the Most Merciful unseen and came with a heart that constantly returns to Him.

body.text: The verses describe Paradise being brought near to the God-conscious until it is not far, then mention the qualities of its people: everyone who often turns back to Allah, who guards His limits, who feared the Most Merciful unseen, and who came to his Lord with a heart turning in repentance.

وَأُزْلِفَتِ الْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ
هَٰذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ
مَنْ خَشِيَ الرَّحْمَٰنَ بِالْغَيْبِ وَجَاءَ بِقَلْبٍ مُنِيبٍ

The one who often turns back is not someone who never errs, but someone who returns again and again whenever he errs, and the repentant heart is one that comes back to its Lord in every state. Reflect on His words «who feared the Most Merciful unseen»: fear is joined to the name the Most Merciful, for the believer's fear of his Lord is blended with hope in His mercy. So make returning a habit: seeking forgiveness after every slip, and moments of solitude in which you review your heart.

en.title: Be Just; That Is Nearer to Piety
en.excerpt: Do not let your dislike of someone lead you to wrong him; justice is a right even for opponents.

body.text: The verse forbids the believers from letting hatred of a people lead them to abandon justice towards them, and affirms that justice is nearer to piety. The real test of justice is not with those you love, but with those with whom you have a dispute.

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَاءَ بِالْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا ۚ اعْدِلُوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ

When you disagree with someone, watch your tongue and your judgment of him: do not attribute to him what he did not say, do not deny his merits, and do not take pleasure in exaggerating your criticism of him. Fairness in a dispute is the sign of a God-conscious soul, and it is what protects your religion from being dragged by anger into injustice.

en.title: Give Us Good in This World and Good in the Hereafter
en.excerpt: A comprehensive supplication that gathers the good of this world and the next and salvation from the Fire in a few words.

body.text: Allah mentions a group of people who combine in their supplication a request for good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and ask Him for protection from the punishment of the Fire. Their supplication was balanced, neither neglecting this world nor forgetting the Hereafter.
وَمِنۡهُم مَّن يَقُولُ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا حَسَنَةٗ وَفِي ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ حَسَنَةٗ وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ

Islam does not ask you to abandon this world, but to ask Allah for its good while you work for the Hereafter. So make this supplication one of the things you repeat most, for it includes health, provision, a righteous spouse and knowledge, and in the Hereafter it includes Allah's pleasure, Paradise and salvation from the Fire.

en.title: He Has Subjected to You Whatever Is in the Heavens and the Earth
en.excerpt: Everything around you has been made subservient to you by Allah; have you made that a path to thanking Him?

body.text: The verse recalls an all-encompassing blessing: Allah has made subservient to man what is in the heavens, the sun, moon and stars, and what is in the earth, rivers, trees and more, all of it from Him as a bounty and kindness. In that are signs for a people who reflect.
وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمْ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا مِنْهُ ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

The phrase «all from Him» returns every blessing to its source: the light you work by, the food you eat and the road you walk on are all from Allah. So when you benefit from something, remember the Giver before you mention the means.

Subjection is a trust, not a licence for domination. Whoever knows that things were made subservient to him by his Lord uses them in His obedience, neither wasting nor spoiling them, and makes his reflection on them a door to increased faith. So ask yourself with every blessing: has this brought me closer to my Lord or taken me further from Him?

en.title: Those Who Are Constant in Their Prayer
en.excerpt: Being constant in prayer is a fortress that protects the soul from anxiety and panic.

body.text: The preceding verses state that man was created anxious, impatient when evil touches him and withholding when good comes to him, and then they make an exception for those who pray. It is as if constant prayer were the remedy for this weakness ingrained in the soul.

إِلَّا ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ
ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِهِمْ دَآئِمُونَ

Constancy means that prayer is fixed in your day and does not change with changing circumstances: in joy and sorrow, in travel and at home, in energy and fatigue. If you feel anxious or unsettled, do not make prayer the last thing you turn to, but the first; standing before Allah five times a day rearranges the heart and calms its fear.

en.title: And You Became, by His Favour, Brothers
en.excerpt: Harmony between hearts is a blessing from Allah, preserved by holding fast to His rope and avoiding division.

body.text: The verse commands the believers to hold fast to the rope of Allah all together and forbids division. It reminds them of His blessing upon them when they were enemies and He brought their hearts together, so that by His favour they became brothers after having been on the brink of a pit of fire.

وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا ۚ وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ كُنْتُمْ أَعْدَاءً فَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِكُمْ فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ بِنِعْمَتِهِ إِخْوَانًا وَكُنْتُمْ عَلَىٰ شَفَا حُفْرَةٍ مِنَ النَّارِ فَأَنْقَذَكُمْ مِنْهَا ۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ

The brotherhood that unites hearts is not the fruit of human effort alone; it is a blessing from Allah that deserves gratitude and protection. Just as the ummah preserves its unity by holding fast to the rope of Allah, the family preserves its cohesion by returning to His command in disagreements and abandoning the causes of division such as backbiting and competing over worldly things. So remember the blessing of harmony in your home, and take care never to be a cause of its division.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 103

en.title: Do Not Fear and Do Not Grieve
en.excerpt: A command that seemed frightening on the surface was in reality the path to safety for Musa (peace be upon him).

body.text: The mother of Musa fears for her infant, and Allah inspires her to cast him into the river if she fears for him, reassuring her with two great promises: that he will be returned to her, and that he will be among the messengers. It is one of the tenderest scenes of motherhood in the Qur'an.
وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ ۖ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِي الْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِي وَلَا تَحْزَنِي ۖ إِنَّا رَادُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ

Allah may command His servant with something that appears frightening, yet all the good lies in it. True reliance is to obey Allah's command while certain that His arrangement is more merciful to you than your own arrangement for yourself. Reflect on how Allah combined for the mother of Musa the removal of fear for the future and of grief over the separation, and then gave her a promise to hold on to. Likewise, in hardships the heart needs Allah's promise to hold on to until it sees relief.

en.title: We Will Show Them Our Signs in the Horizons and Within Themselves
en.excerpt: Allah's signs are scattered across the universe and within the soul, and the more a person reflects on them, the more certain he becomes of the truth.

body.text: A promise from Allah that He will show people His signs in the vast horizons around them and within their own selves close at hand, until it becomes clear to them that what the Qur'an brought is the truth; and Allah suffices as a Witness over all things.
سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ ۗ أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ

The path to certainty has two wings: looking at the vast universe, and looking at the self with its wonders of creation, perception and feeling. Both are an open book for whoever wishes to read. The more you look, the more certain you become.

Set aside time to contemplate a sky, a sea, or your own body that works without your commanding it, then ask yourself: who arranged this? Such contemplation revives faith and turns it into firm certainty rather than mere information.

en.title: A Sincere Repentance
en.excerpt: Sincere repentance is truthful and pure; it mends what has passed and lights the way to what is to come.

body.text: Allah calls the believers to sincere repentance, promising them the removal of their misdeeds and entry into gardens, and describes their state on the Day of Resurrection: their light running before them and on their right, as they ask their Lord to perfect their light for them and to forgive them.

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا تُوبُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يُكَفِّرَ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَيُدْخِلَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ يَوْمَ لَا يُخْزِي اللَّهُ النَّبِيَّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ ۖ نُورُهُمْ يَسْعَىٰ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمَانِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

Sincere repentance is pure and truthful: regret over what has passed, giving up the sin, and resolving never to return to it. Notice that the address is directed to the believers; repentance is not only for sinners but is the believer's constant state. Even the people of light on the Day of Resurrection say «perfect our light for us» and ask for forgiveness; no servant can ever do without his Lord's pardon.

en.title: Indeed, the Covenant Will Be Questioned About
en.excerpt: Every promise you make you will be asked about, so do not promise except what you will fulfil.

body.text: The verse brings together protecting the orphan's wealth and fulfilling one's covenant, then reminds us that the covenant will be asked about. The word a person commits himself to does not end when the gathering ends; it remains in his record until he is asked about it.
وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ ۚ وَأَوْفُوا بِالْعَهْدِ ۖ إِنَّ الْعَهْدَ كَانَ مَسْئُولًا

So review your commitments: the contracts you have signed, the appointments you have set, and the promises you have made to your family and friends. Write down what you fear forgetting, and apologise for what you cannot do before its time comes. Keeping in mind that you will be questioned makes a person more careful with his words and less hasty in making promises.

en.title: Our Lord, Pour Upon Us Patience
en.excerpt: Before facing the enemy, the believers first asked for patience and steadfastness, and then for victory.

body.text: When Talut and the believers with him went out to face Jalut and his soldiers and saw the great number of the enemy, they turned to Allah, asking Him to pour patience upon them, to make their feet firm, and to grant them victory over the disbelieving people.
وَلَمَّا بَرَزُواْ لِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦ قَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ أَفۡرِغۡ عَلَيۡنَا صَبۡرٗا وَثَبِّتۡ أَقۡدَامَنَا وَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ

In difficult situations you need inner strength before anything else. So if you face an exam, an illness or a hardship, ask Allah first for patience and steadfastness, for they are the key to relief. And know that a few who seek Allah's help are stronger than a multitude deluded by itself.

en.title: So Do Not Claim Purity for Yourselves
en.excerpt: Allah has known you best since you were an embryo; so do not praise yourself, and busy yourself with reforming it.

body.text: The verse describes the doers of good as those who avoid the major sins and indecencies, recalls the vastness of Allah's forgiveness, and then affirms that He knows people best since He produced them from the earth and when they were embryos in the wombs, so they should not claim purity for themselves; He knows best who is God-conscious.

الَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَالْفَوَاحِشَ إِلَّا اللَّمَمَ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَاسِعُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ ۚ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِكُمْ إِذْ أَنْشَأَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ وَإِذْ أَنْتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ ۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ ۖ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اتَّقَىٰ

Part of perfect faith in Allah's knowledge is that the servant be humble: the One who knew you «when you were embryos» knows your inner self better than you do. So do not praise yourself excessively or be deluded by your deeds; think well of others, and leave the judgment of hearts to Allah.

In His words «Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness» is an open door of hope: if you slip, do not despair, but hasten to repent, combining hope in His forgiveness with shyness before His knowledge. Between these two wings the believer travels to his Lord, neither feeling secure nor despairing, but working and hoping.

en.title: Stand in Prayer by Night, Except a Little
en.excerpt: Night prayer and measured recitation of the Qur'an are provisions that strengthen the believer for the burdens of the day.

body.text: At the beginning of Surah Al-Muzzammil comes a command to stand in prayer at night, with ease granted in its amount, half the night, or a little more or less, followed by a command to recite the Qur'an in measured tones. The night is a time for being alone with Allah and receiving His words slowly.

قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
نِصْفَهُ أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا
أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا

You are not required to start with long hours. Begin with two units of prayer before you sleep or before Fajr, reciting slowly what you have memorised, then increase little by little. Measured recitation is not just beautifying the voice; it is a slowness that gives the heart a chance to understand. Reading one page with reflection is better for your heart than reading whole sections without presence.

en.title: My Lord, Enable Me to Be Grateful for Your Favour
en.excerpt: When a person reaches maturity, he gathers his parents, his descendants and himself in his supplication.

body.text: The verse describes the mother's hardship in pregnancy and childbirth, then turns to man when he reaches full strength and forty years, as he calls upon his Lord to enable him to be grateful for His favour upon him and upon his parents, and to make his descendants righteous for him.

وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۖ حَمَلَتۡهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرۡهٗا وَوَضَعَتۡهُ كُرۡهٗاۖ وَحَمۡلُهُۥ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ ثَلَٰثُونَ شَهۡرًاۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَبَلَغَ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةٗ قَالَ رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِيٓ أَنۡ أَشۡكُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَيَّ وَأَنۡ أَعۡمَلَ صَٰلِحٗا تَرۡضَىٰهُ وَأَصۡلِحۡ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِيٓۖ إِنِّي تُبۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ

In the middle of life a person stands between two generations: parents whose virtue he now sees clearly, and children whose righteousness he hopes for. The verse teaches him to gather both generations in a single supplication and to join it with repentance and righteous deeds. So memorise this supplication and repeat it, and remember that the righteousness of your descendants begins with your own gratitude and your own deeds.

en.title: What Will You Worship After Me?
en.excerpt: In his final moments, Yaqub did not ask about wealth; he made sure of his sons' faith.

body.text: When death approached Yaqub (peace be upon him), he gathered his sons and asked them a single question that revealed what concerned his heart most: what will you worship after I am gone? They answered him with what delighted his eyes: affirmation of Allah's oneness and submission to Him.

أَمۡ كُنتُمۡ شُهَدَآءَ إِذۡ حَضَرَ يَعۡقُوبَ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ إِذۡ قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعۡبُدُونَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِيۖ قَالُواْ نَعۡبُدُ إِلَٰهَكَ وَإِلَٰهَ ءَابَآئِكَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ إِلَٰهٗا وَٰحِدٗا وَنَحۡنُ لَهُۥ مُسۡلِمُونَ

The greatest thing a parent leaves to his children is not a material inheritance but firmly rooted faith. In the last moments of his life, Yaqub (peace be upon him) gave no instructions about trade or money; he made sure that his sons would worship «One God». So let the concern of fathers and mothers be to plant in their children the love and worship of Allah, and to follow up on it through questions and conversation until the end of life. Righteous descendants who worship Allah alone are a continuation of good after a person departs.

en.title: You See the Earth Still, but When We Send Down Rain upon It
en.excerpt: Just as the lifeless earth comes alive with rain, dead hearts come alive with the remembrance of Allah and His mercy.

body.text: The verse depicts a barren earth with no vegetation; when water comes down upon it, it stirs and swells. It then makes this a proof that the One who gave it life is able to give life to the dead, and He has power over all things.
وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنَّكَ تَرَى الْأَرْضَ خَاشِعَةً فَإِذَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا الْمَاءَ اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ ۚ إِنَّ الَّذِي أَحْيَاهَا لَمُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ ۚ إِنَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

The scene holds hope for every soul that has felt dry: do not despair of your heart however long its hardness has lasted, for the One who revives the earth after its death is able to revive faith and humility in you anew. No heart is further from Allah's mercy than a dead land that He brought back to life.

Seek rain for your heart: sincere supplication, reflective recitation, righteous company and renewed repentance. Then wait for it to «stir and swell» within you, for Allah's way of giving life never fails. And be patient: the rain may be delayed, but it comes.

en.title: Every Soul Is Held in Pledge for What It Has Earned
en.excerpt: Your deeds are what hold you captive or set you free; so strive to free yourself through righteous deeds.

body.text: A short verse carrying a great meaning: every soul is held in pledge for the deeds it has earned, just as a pledge is held by its owner. Either its deeds will ruin and destroy it, or they will free it and rescue it from ruin.
كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ

No one will carry your deeds for you, and neither lineage nor status will benefit you if you do not have what releases your pledge. This calls you to personal responsibility: to hold yourself to account before you are held to account, and to hasten to righteous deeds and repentance. Every act of obedience is a step towards freeing yourself, and every delay lengthens your chains.

en.title: Repel Evil with That Which Is Better
en.excerpt: Meeting harm with kindness extinguishes enmity and keeps the heart pure.

body.text: The verse points to a refined way of facing harm: to repel the bad deed with the trait that is better, whether pardon, a kind word or forbearance, with the certainty that Allah knows best what the wrongdoers say, so there is no need for revenge.
ٱدْفَعْ بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ ۚ نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَصِفُونَ

If someone wrongs you, ask yourself: what is the best response I can offer here? It may be wise silence, an apology no one asked for, or a kindness that surprises the wrongdoer. Trust that Allah knows what was said about you, leave the reckoning to Him, and protect your heart from rancour.

en.title: My Lord, Grant Me from Yourself Good Offspring
en.excerpt: Zakariya did not ask merely for a child; he asked for good, righteous offspring.

body.text: When Zakariya (peace be upon him) saw Allah's honour to Maryam and how He provided for her without measure, it moved him to supplicate. He asked his Lord to grant him from Himself good offspring, appealing to Him through the fact that He is the Hearer of supplication.
هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُ ۖ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً ۖ إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ

When you ask Allah for children, ask Him for their righteousness before their number, for good offspring are a comfort to the eyes in this world and a treasure in the Hereafter. Learn from Zakariya that seeing Allah's blessings upon others should open the door of hope and supplication, not the door of envy and comparison.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 38

en.title: No Secret of Yours Will Remain Hidden
en.excerpt: A day on which everything will be exposed; so set your private self right today as you set right your public self.

body.text: The verse describes a scene from the Day of Resurrection: people are presented before their Lord, and nothing of them is hidden from Allah, however minute or concealed it may be; rather, He knows it and is fully aware of it.
يَوْمَئِذٍ تُعْرَضُونَ لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنْكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ

Faith in the Last Day changes a person's behaviour in private, for what he hides today will one day be exposed, «no secret of yours will remain hidden». So keep good secrets: a hidden charity, units of prayer no one sees, and supplication for your brothers in their absence.

This verse is also a consolation for the wronged: whatever of his right was lost in this world will not be lost there. So let him be patient and seek reward, knowing that being presented before Allah is complete justice. Whoever is certain of this presentation wrongs no one, carries no rancour in his heart that drives him to revenge, and leaves the reckoning to the One from whom no secret is hidden.

en.title: And Bow with Those Who Bow
en.excerpt: Prayer, zakah and congregation: worship that connects you to your Lord and connects you to your brothers.

body.text: This verse gathers three commands in a single line: establishing prayer, giving zakah, and bowing with those who bow. Worship in Islam is not an isolated individual affair, but a life shared with the community of believers.
وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱرۡكَعُواْ مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ

His words «with those who bow» are an invitation to be part of the row, standing shoulder to shoulder with your brothers, so that you feel you are not alone on your path to Allah. So be keen to attend the congregational prayer as much as you can, for a single row teaches humility, dissolves differences and strengthens resolve for obedience.

en.title: By Mutual Consent and Consultation
en.excerpt: Even in the small affairs of an infant, the Qur'an guided parents to mutual consent and consultation.

body.text: The verse sets out the rulings on nursing: mothers nurse their children for two full years; the father is responsible for their provision and clothing in a fair manner; neither parent should be made to suffer because of their child; and weaning before two years should be by mutual consent and consultation between them.

وَٱلۡوَٰلِدَٰتُ يُرۡضِعۡنَ أَوۡلَٰدَهُنَّ حَوۡلَيۡنِ كَامِلَيۡنِۖ لِمَنۡ أَرَادَ أَن يُتِمَّ ٱلرَّضَاعَةَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلۡمَوۡلُودِ لَهُۥ رِزۡقُهُنَّ وَكِسۡوَتُهُنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ لَا تُكَلَّفُ نَفۡسٌ إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۚ لَا تُضَآرَّ وَٰلِدَةُۢ بِوَلَدِهَا وَلَا مَوۡلُودٞ لَّهُۥ بِوَلَدِهِۦۚ وَعَلَى ٱلۡوَارِثِ مِثۡلُ ذَٰلِكَۗ فَإِنۡ أَرَادَا فِصَالًا عَن تَرَاضٖ مِّنۡهُمَا وَتَشَاوُرٖ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِمَاۗ وَإِنۡ أَرَدتُّمۡ أَن تَسۡتَرۡضِعُوٓاْ أَوۡلَٰدَكُمۡ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذَا سَلَّمۡتُم مَّآ ءَاتَيۡتُم بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٞ

Raising a child is a shared responsibility, not one that either parent takes on alone, and its decisions should not be made in an atmosphere of stubbornness. The verse forbids using the child as a means of harming the other party, and makes consultation and mutual consent the method, even after separation. If you disagree on a matter concerning your children, put their interest first, talk calmly, and remember that Allah sees what you do.

en.title: In the Name of Allah Is Its Course and Its Anchorage
en.excerpt: Nuh begins the journey of salvation in the name of Allah, making all movement and stillness in His name.

body.text: Nuh (peace be upon him) commands those who believed with him to board the ship while the waves are mighty and danger surrounds them. He does not rely on the sturdiness of the ship alone, but makes its sailing and its anchoring in the name of Allah, and reminds them of His forgiveness and mercy.
وَقَالَ ارْكَبُوا فِيهَا بِسْمِ اللَّهِ مَجْرَاهَا وَمُرْسَاهَا ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ

Beginning every matter in the name of Allah connects the work to its Creator and seeks blessing and protection from Him. Nuh (peace be upon him) built the ship with his own hands, yet he did not rely on his craftsmanship; rather, he made its course and its stopping «in the name of Allah».

So let this spirit be present in your travels and when driving your car, and at the start of your work, studies and projects: put your effort into preparation, then begin in the name of Allah, and ask Him to grant you safety in setting out and in arriving.

en.title: It Is He Who Sent Down Tranquility into the Hearts of the Believers
en.excerpt: Tranquility is a gift from Allah that He sends down upon the hearts of the believers, increasing them in faith and steadfastness.

body.text: The verse tells us that tranquility is a blessing Allah sends down into the hearts of the believers so that they may increase in faith along with their faith, that to Allah belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, and that He is All-Knowing, All-Wise. It is a verse that brings reassurance to every anxious heart.
هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ السَّكِينَةَ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لِيَزْدَادُوا إِيمَانًا مَعَ إِيمَانِهِمْ ۗ وَلِلَّهِ جُنُودُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۚ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا

Tranquility cannot be bought, nor produced by psychological tricks alone; it is sought from Allah, who owns the hearts. When it descends upon the heart, the heart stands firm in hardships and becomes better able to make the right decision. It is a gift sought through supplication and closeness to Him.

So if your soul is troubled, ask Allah for tranquility in word and meaning, hold to what brings you closer to Him, and remember that Allah has soldiers you do not know, which He puts at the service of whomever He wills of His servants, by His knowledge and wisdom. Those soldiers serve His command, and His command is all good for His believing servants.

en.title: And Fear a Day When You Will Be Returned
en.excerpt: A day on which you will be returned to Allah and repaid your deeds in full; so give it a place in your daily reckoning.

body.text: The verse calls us to guard against a tremendous day on which people will be returned to Allah, and then every soul will be repaid in full what it earned, without any deduction, and they will not be wronged. Nothing will be added to a wrongdoer, and nothing taken away from a doer of good.
وَٱتَّقُواْ يَوۡمٗا تُرۡجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ ثُمَّ تُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفۡسٖ مَّا كَسَبَتۡ وَهُمۡ لَا يُظۡلَمُونَ

When the believer keeps this day in mind, his view of his small dealings changes: in buying and selling, in debts and in people's rights. What seems trivial today will be repaid in full tomorrow. So pause before every decision and ask yourself: how will I meet Allah with this? In that question lies protection from many errors.

en.title: They Walk upon the Earth Humbly
en.excerpt: A calm gait and a peaceful word are among the qualities of the servants of the Most Merciful.

body.text: The verse opens the description of the servants of the Most Merciful with two traits: humility in walking, without arrogance or swagger, and responding to the ignorant with words that keep them safe from sin. Outward calm reflects inner tranquility.
وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمۡشُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ هَوۡنٗا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلۡجَٰهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلَٰمٗا

When someone provokes you with ignorant words, do not descend to their level; say something peaceful that ends the argument and preserves your dignity. In your walking and movement be humble and calm, neither pushing nor acting superior. These small manners make those around you feel safe in your company.

en.title: Forgive Us Our Sins and Our Excesses in Our Affairs
en.excerpt: In the hour of hardship, the followers of the prophets blamed no one; they began by seeking forgiveness for their own sins.

body.text: The verse describes the state of the sincere believers who were with their prophets when they were struck by what struck them in the cause of Allah: their only words were a request for forgiveness of their sins and of their excesses in their affairs, followed by a request for steadfastness and victory.
وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسْرَافَنَا فِي أَمْرِنَا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا وَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ

When a calamity befalls you, begin by examining yourself before blaming others, for sins may be a cause of delayed relief. Seeking forgiveness opens the door to steadfastness and victory, as in the order of this supplication: forgiveness first, then steadfastness, then victory.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 147

en.title: Did He Not Find You an Orphan and Give You Refuge?
en.excerpt: Remember how Allah cared for you in the past, and you will be at peace about His care in what is to come.

body.text: Allah enumerates three blessings upon His Prophet: He found him an orphan and gave him refuge, found him unaware of the Book and of faith and guided him, and found him poor and made him self-sufficient. It is a reminder that divine care came first and continues.

أَلَمۡ يَجِدۡكَ يَتِيمٗا فَـَٔاوَىٰ
وَوَجَدَكَ ضَآلّٗا فَهَدَىٰ
وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلٗا فَأَغۡنَىٰ

One of the most helpful ways to strengthen trust in Allah is to review your history with Him: how many times did things become tight for you and then open up? How many needs were fulfilled from where you never expected? So take a moment to count these situations, for the One who sheltered you, guided you and enriched you will not let you be lost.

The order of the verses also trains one in gratitude: whoever remembers his former state knows the worth of the blessing, and has mercy on those going through what he went through, so he becomes a support for the orphan, the one who asks, and the needy. Part of being grateful for a blessing is being a means of it reaching others, as it once reached you.

en.title: And Before Dawn They Would Seek Forgiveness
en.excerpt: The time before dawn is a precious appointment for seeking forgiveness, one that many people neglect.

body.text: These two verses describe the doers of good as those who used to sleep but little of the night, and then close their night by seeking forgiveness before dawn. They strive in worship and then seek forgiveness as though they had fallen short.

كَانُواْ قَلِيلٗا مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ مَا يَهۡجَعُونَ
وَبِٱلۡأَسۡحَارِ هُمۡ يَسۡتَغۡفِرُونَ

This is a lesson in humility: worship does not make its doer arrogant; rather, it increases his sense of falling short before Allah's greatness, so he turns to seeking forgiveness. If you wake before Fajr, even a little, make those minutes a fixed appointment for seeking forgiveness; they are quiet moments in which the heart is free of distractions and clear for intimate prayer.

en.title: We Made You Peoples and Tribes That You May Know One Another
en.excerpt: The diversity of peoples and tribes is for knowing and befriending one another, and true honour lies in piety.

body.text: Allah addresses all people, saying that He created them from a male and a female and made them peoples and tribes so that they may know one another. He then affirms that the most noble of them in His sight is the most God-conscious, not the wealthiest nor the one of highest lineage.
يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَائِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوا ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ

The single origin makes humanity one large family, and the diversity among them is a door to getting to know one another and cooperating, not to boasting and estrangement. So teach your children to respect people of all origins and languages, and instil in them that a person's worth lies in his piety and character, not in his colour or his family.

en.title: O Ants, Enter Your Dwellings
en.excerpt: A tiny ant feels responsible for her community, warns them, and makes excuses for others.

body.text: Sulayman (peace be upon him) passes with his soldiers by the valley of the ants. An ant hastens to warn her community of the approaching danger, commands them to enter their dwellings, and excuses the soldiers by saying that they do not perceive it.
حَتَّىٰ إِذَا أَتَوْا عَلَىٰ وَادِ النَّمْلِ قَالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ لَا يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ سُلَيْمَانُ وَجُنُودُهُ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ

The ant's stance holds lessons in responsibility: she saw the danger and did not save herself alone, but called out to all her community and guided them to the practical solution in clear, concise words. Every individual can benefit his community according to what he sees and knows. And of her good manners, she made an excuse for Sulayman and his soldiers, saying «while they do not perceive», not accusing them of intending harm. So should we think well of people, and warn of danger without accusing intentions.

en.title: Is It You Who Make It Grow, or Are We the Grower?
en.excerpt: Man ploughs and sows, but making it sprout and bringing it forth is in Allah's hand alone.

body.text: The verses ask man a question that awakens awareness: have you considered what you sow? Is it you who make it grow, or is it Allah who makes it grow? Had He willed, He would have made it dry debris, leaving its owner regretful and bewildered. In this question is a gentle reminder of the limits of human power.

أَفَرَءَيْتُم مَّا تَحْرُثُونَ
ءَأَنتُمْ تَزْرَعُونَهُۥٓ أَمْ نَحْنُ ٱلزَّٰرِعُونَ
لَوْ نَشَآءُ لَجَعَلْنَٰهُ حُطَٰمًۭا فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ

Human effort is a required means, but the result is in Allah's hand. The farmer places the seed, yet he cannot bring forth from it a stalk or a fruit; and so it is with every endeavour in life: you sow and Allah makes it grow. Success is from Allah first and last.

So do not be deluded by your effort when you succeed, nor despair when the fruit is delayed. Work with excellence, then attribute the credit to its true Owner, and thank Him for the fruits He brought forth from your work. In this way you combine diligence and humility.

en.title: Indeed We Belong to Allah, and to Him We Shall Return
en.excerpt: A phrase that reminds you in calamity that you and all you own belong to Allah, and that the return is to Him.

body.text: The two verses describe the patient, who, when a calamity strikes them, say: «Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we shall return». They give them glad tidings that upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy, and that they are the ones rightly guided to truth and what is correct.

ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَٰبَتۡهُم مُّصِيبَةٞ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيۡهِ رَٰجِعُونَ
أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ صَلَوَٰتٞ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ وَرَحۡمَةٞۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدُونَ

This phrase holds a remedy for the stricken heart: «we belong to Allah» is a reminder that we are His possession and that what was taken from us was only on loan to us; «and to Him we shall return» is a reminder that the meeting is near and that separation is not the end. So do not let it be a phrase said only with the tongue, but a meaning held in the heart, so that you attain what Allah has promised the patient.

en.title: Let Them Pardon and Overlook
en.excerpt: Whoever loves for Allah to forgive him should forgive those who wronged him.

body.text: The verse forbids people of virtue and means from swearing to cut off their kindness to their relatives and the needy because of a wrong that occurred, and then asks a question that touches the heart: do you not love that Allah should forgive you? Pardoning people is a path to Allah's pardon.

وَلَا يَأْتَلِ أُولُو الْفَضْلِ مِنْكُمْ وَالسَّعَةِ أَنْ يُؤْتُوا أُولِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينَ وَالْمُهَاجِرِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ۖ وَلْيَعْفُوا وَلْيَصْفَحُوا ۗ أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ

If a relative hurts you, do not cut off your kindness to him, and do not let the wrong be a reason to stop the good. Pardon by not holding it against him, and overlook by erasing its trace from your heart, keeping in mind your own need for Allah's forgiveness. Just as you love for Allah to pass over your slips, pass over the slips of others.

en.title: My Lord, Make Me an Establisher of Prayer, and from My Descendants
en.excerpt: Ibrahim asks for steadfastness in prayer for himself and his descendants, then forgiveness for himself, his parents and the believers.

body.text: In the supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), he asks his Lord to make him one who establishes prayer properly, and to make among his descendants those who establish it. He then asks that his supplication be accepted, and for forgiveness for himself, his parents and the believers on the Day of Reckoning.

رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي ۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ
رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْحِسَابُ

Establishing prayer is a gift of success from Allah to be asked of Him, not merely a habit. So pray for yourself and your children to keep it up, and do not forget your parents and the believers in your supplication. This supplication teaches you to widen the circle of your mercy to include those who came before you and those who will come after you.

en.title: To Allah Belongs the Dominion of the Heavens and the Earth
en.excerpt: What is in your hand is on loan from its true Owner; so use it in what pleases Him.

body.text: Surah Al-Ma'idah closes by affirming that the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all within them belongs to Allah alone; He is their Creator and the Disposer of their affairs, and He has power over all things, with nothing beyond Him. It is a conclusion that gathers the meanings of the surah in affirming Allah's absolute dominion.
لِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا فِيهِنَّ ۚ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

When you know that all dominion belongs to Allah, the world becomes easy to bear when it slips away, and you do not transgress through it when it comes to you. You are a steward over what is in your hands, not its owner in reality. So spend from it and do good, for it is His wealth, which He gives to whom He wills.

The verse's ending, «has power over all things», is an invitation to hope: however complicated your affair may seem, it is not difficult for Allah. So knock on His door with supplication, certain of His power, and do not let the weakness of the means weaken your hope, for the All-Powerful is not limited by means.

en.title: And Part of the Night, Pray Tahajjud as an Extra for You
en.excerpt: Tahajjud is a voluntary prayer by which the servant rises to lofty stations with his Lord.

body.text: After the command to perform the obligatory prayers came the command to pray tahajjud at night as an additional voluntary act, with the promise of a praiseworthy station. Voluntary acts are a ladder by which the servant rises once he has perfected the obligations. Herein is glad tidings for everyone who stands in prayer at night.
وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَتَهَجَّدْ بِهِ نَافِلَةً لَكَ عَسَىٰ أَنْ يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقَامًا مَحْمُودًا

There is a wise order here: begin by perfecting your obligations, then add to them whatever voluntary acts you can keep up consistently, for a little that is constant is more beloved than much that is interrupted. Know that every voluntary act of worship has an effect in raising your rank, so do not deprive yourself of a few units of prayer in the depth of the night, hoping that Allah will raise you to a station He is pleased with for you.

en.title: And Gives Wealth, Despite Loving It, to Relatives
en.excerpt: Part of the reality of righteousness is giving your wealth while you love it, and beginning with your relatives.

body.text: The verse explains that righteousness is not merely facing a direction in prayer, but sincere faith that shows in conduct, and among its first forms is giving wealth, despite loving it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the wayfarer and those who ask.

لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ قِبَلَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِي ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُوفُونَ بِعَهۡدِهِمۡ إِذَا عَٰهَدُواْۖ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ فِي ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلۡبَأۡسِۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَ

Mentioning relatives first draws attention to the fact that those most deserving of your kindness are your family and needy relatives; so do not let your giving to those far away come at the expense of those close to you. His words «despite loving it» remind us that the value of giving lies in genuine self-sacrifice; so give from what you love, even if it is little, for it is heavier on the scale and truer in faith.

en.title: To Test Me Whether I Will Be Grateful or Ungrateful
en.excerpt: Sulayman saw in his great blessing a test of his gratitude, not proof that he deserved it.

body.text: The throne of the Queen of Sheba is brought to Sulayman (peace be upon him) in the blink of an eye. He does not meet this wondrous event with pride; rather, he says at once that this is from the favour of his Lord, and that it is a test to see whether he will be grateful or ungrateful.

قَالَ الَّذِي عِنْدَهُ عِلْمٌ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ أَنَا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْتَدَّ إِلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ ۚ فَلَمَّا رَآهُ مُسْتَقِرًّا عِنْدَهُ قَالَ هَٰذَا مِنْ فَضْلِ رَبِّي لِيَبْلُوَنِي أَأَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ ۖ وَمَنْ شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ ۖ وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ

Blessings are not mere gifts; they are a test. Whoever sees Allah's blessing upon him in his health, wealth or position should ask himself: am I thanking this blessing by using it in obedience to Allah, or am I forgetting it and attributing the credit to myself? The verse makes clear that gratitude benefits the one who is grateful, «he is grateful only for his own good», and that Allah is free of need of His creation's thanks. The grateful one is the winner: your gratitude preserves the blessing and increases it, and keeps your heart connected to the Giver.

en.title: And He Is with You Wherever You Are
en.excerpt: Being mindful that Allah is with you by His knowledge everywhere sets your private self right and comforts you in solitude.

body.text: After mentioning the creation of the heavens and the earth, and Allah's knowledge of what enters the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the sky and what ascends into it, the verse brings the meaning close to man's heart: «And He is with you».

هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا وَمَا يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وَمَا يَعْرُجُ فِيهَا ۖ وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ

The Allah whose knowledge encompasses the entire universe knows your state in your home, your work and your solitude. This meaning gives the believer companionship in his loneliness, and a modesty that keeps him from sin when no one sees him. He is near to whoever calls upon Him, and no secret is hidden from Him.

Set aside moments in your day to be mindful of this nearness: when you are alone with your phone, when you are angry, and when you are weak. And remember that the verse ends by saying that Allah sees what you do, so do your deeds well, for they are seen by your Lord.

en.title: Except One Who Comes to Allah with a Sound Heart
en.excerpt: On a day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, the sound heart alone remains the servant's capital.

body.text: These two verses come in the supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) as he mentions the Day of Resurrection: a day on which neither wealth nor children will benefit, except whoever comes to his Lord with a sound heart. There, every scale falls away except the scale of the heart.

يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌۭ وَلَا بَنُونَ
إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى ٱللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍۢ سَلِيمٍۢ

The sound heart is one that is free of polytheism and doubt, and of hatred, envy and all other diseases of the heart. We care a great deal for our bodies and our wealth, yet seldom check on our hearts. So give your heart special care: an intention to correct, a grudge to remove, and remembrance to revive it, for it is the one thing you will carry with you to your Lord.

en.title: The Strong and the Trustworthy
en.excerpt: Competence and trustworthiness together are the standard for choosing whom we entrust with work.

body.text: The daughter of the righteous old man suggested to her father that he hire Musa (peace be upon him), giving as her reason that the best one to hire is the strong and trustworthy. In a short phrase she captured a fair standard for choosing whom to entrust with work.
قَالَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا يَا أَبَتِ اسْتَأْجِرْهُ ۖ إِنَّ خَيْرَ مَنِ اسْتَأْجَرْتَ الْقَوِيُّ الْأَمِينُ

Strength alone without trustworthiness wastes rights, and trustworthiness alone without ability wastes the work. So strive to be in your work both strong and skilful, and trustworthy and honest. When you choose an employee or a partner, do not settle for one of the two qualities; look for both together.

en.title: Cause Me to Enter a Sound Entrance and Exit a Sound Exit
en.excerpt: A supplication fitting for every beginning and ending: a new job, a journey, or a stage of life.

body.text: Allah teaches His Prophet ﷺ to ask Him that his entry into every matter and his exit from it be with truthfulness, goodness and contentment, and that He grant him from Himself a supporting authority by which He helps him.
وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ وَاجْعَلْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ سُلْطَانًا نَصِيرًا

Before you begin new work or move to a new place or stage, ask Allah that your entry and exit be with truthfulness and a good intention. Good beginnings make good endings, and whoever has Allah as his Helper is not harmed by a lack of means.

en.title: And Worship Your Lord Until Certainty Comes to You
en.excerpt: Worship is not a season that ends; it is a path that continues until death comes to you.

body.text: Surah Al-Hijr closes with a comprehensive command: that the believer persist in worshipping his Lord and continue in it as long as he lives, until certainty comes to him, which is death, whose coming is beyond doubt.
وَاعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَكَ الْيَقِينُ

The verse holds a cure for slackness: worship is not tied to a stage of life or a season of the year, but extends «until certainty comes to you». If you feel weak after a period of energy, do not abandon all your deeds; keep up a small, constant amount that preserves your connection with your Lord.

Calling death «certainty» reminds you that it is the one matter no one doubts, and yet many are heedless of it. So let remembering it be a motive for uprightness, not for sadness, and ask Allah to grant you a good ending while you are obeying Him.

en.title: That They Might Reflect upon Its Verses
en.excerpt: The Qur'an was sent down as a blessed Book to be reflected upon; true recitation begins with understanding.

body.text: This verse explains the purpose of revealing the Qur'an: that people reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding take heed. The full blessing of the Qur'an is attained by pausing at its meanings, not merely by the tongue passing over it.
كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا آيَاتِهِ وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ

So set aside time in your daily portion for reflection: read a verse or two, then read their brief explanation, and ask yourself: what does this verse ask of me today? You will find that the Qur'an speaks to your situation and your worries, and opens doors of understanding for you every time you return to it; and that is the blessing with which Allah described it.

en.title: If You Mix with Them, They Are Your Brothers
en.excerpt: The orphan in your home is a brother whose affairs you set right, not a burden to avoid.

body.text: The Companions asked about how to deal with the orphans in their care, and the answer came that setting their affairs right is best, and that mixing with them in daily living is permitted because they are your brothers, and Allah knows the one who corrupts from the one who sets right.

فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۗ وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰۖ قُلۡ إِصۡلَاحٞ لَّهُمۡ خَيۡرٞۖ وَإِن تُخَالِطُوهُمۡ فَإِخۡوَٰنُكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُصۡلِحِۚ وَلَوۡ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَعۡنَتَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٞ

The verse removes any hesitation about sponsoring an orphan and living alongside him, and makes intention and setting things right the measure. Let the orphan live within the family as one of them, eating with them and rejoicing with them. Describing them as brothers changes how we see them: they are not cases to pity from afar, but brothers who are owed affection and dignified care.

en.title: May I Follow You So That You Teach Me?
en.excerpt: A prophet to whom Allah spoke seeks knowledge with courtesy and humility; no one is too great to learn.

body.text: Musa (peace be upon him) travels in search of knowledge until he meets the righteous servant. He asks permission to accompany him in a courteous manner, making himself a follower and learner, seeking knowledge that will guide him to what is right.
قَالَ لَهُۥ مُوسَىٰ هَلۡ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ مِمَّا عُلِّمۡتَ رُشۡدٗا

Humility is the key to knowledge. Musa, despite his lofty rank, addressed his teacher by asking permission, made himself a follower, and attributed knowledge to Allah by saying «of what you have been taught». Musa did not seek knowledge for boasting, but sought «right guidance» by which to be guided. So let our seeking of knowledge be with the intention of benefiting and acting, and let our manners with our teachers be a sign of the sincerity of our desire to learn.

en.title: So That You Do Not Grieve over What Has Escaped You
en.excerpt: Certainty in Allah's decree protects the heart from anguish over what is lost and from arrogance over what is present.

body.text: The two verses affirm that every calamity on earth or within ourselves is written before Allah brings it into being, and then explain the wisdom in informing us of this: so that we do not grieve with a crippling grief over what has escaped us, nor rejoice with arrogant joy over what we have been given.

مَا أَصَابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ إِلَّا فِي كِتَابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَبْرَأَهَا ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ
لِكَيْلَا تَأْسَوْا عَلَىٰ مَا فَاتَكُمْ وَلَا تَفْرَحُوا بِمَا آتَاكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتَالٍ فَخُورٍ

Faith in the divine decree is a balance for the emotions: it keeps them from collapsing at loss and from running wild at gain. Its owner lives in balance, grieving a natural grief that does not cripple him and rejoicing a grateful joy that does not make him transgress. This is a great blessing for peace of mind.

If an opportunity passes you by or you lose something, say to yourself: this was written and there is wisdom in it. And if you are given a blessing, be humble, for the verse ends by stating that Allah does not love everyone self-deluded and boastful. Giving and withholding are both in His hand.

en.title: Sincere to Him in Religion
en.excerpt: The root of the whole matter: to worship Allah sincerely, inclining away from everything besides Him.

body.text: The verse sets out the essence of what people were commanded: to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion, inclining away from polytheism towards pure monotheism, to establish prayer and to give zakah; and that is the upright religion.
وَمَا أُمِرُوا إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ حُنَفَاءَ وَيُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُوا الزَّكَاةَ ۚ وَذَٰلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ

Sincerity is the soul of worship. Two prayers may look alike outwardly, yet be far apart in acceptance. That is why sincerity is mentioned in the verse before prayer and zakah. So give your worship a moment of intention before you begin, and know that a little done purely for Allah's sake is better than much done for the sake of something else.

en.title: Then Verify
en.excerpt: Verify before you believe or spread a piece of news, so that you do not wrong anyone and come to regret it.

body.text: The verse sets a great principle for dealing with news: if a report comes from an unreliable source, investigate and verify it, lest you harm a people out of ignorance and then become regretful over what you have done.
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أَنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهَالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلْتُمْ نَادِمِينَ

In the age of forwarded messages and clips taken out of context, this verse is needed more than ever: do not re-send news about a person or an organisation before verifying it, and do not build your judgment of anyone on words you heard about them. How many reputations have been wronged by a word whose transmitter did not verify it, and how much regret could have been avoided by taking one's time.

en.title: And Prepare for Us Right Guidance in Our Affair
en.excerpt: When the earth became narrow for the young men, they took refuge in the cave and in their Lord, asking Him for mercy and right guidance.

body.text: The young believers fled from their people with their faith and took refuge in the cave. They did not ask for wealth or power; rather, they asked Allah for mercy from Himself, and to prepare for them in their affair what would guide them to what is right.
إِذۡ أَوَى ٱلۡفِتۡيَةُ إِلَى ٱلۡكَهۡفِ فَقَالُواْ رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحۡمَةٗ وَهَيِّئۡ لَنَا مِنۡ أَمۡرِنَا رَشَدٗا

In times of confusion and when making big decisions, ask Allah for right guidance before you ask Him for the outcome you want. The good may lie in what you do not expect, and right guidance means that Allah leads you to the best path and then fills your heart with contentment with what He has chosen for you.

en.title: Who Responds to the Distressed When He Calls upon Him?
en.excerpt: When all means are cut off, one door remains that is never closed: the supplication of the distressed.

body.text: The verse asks a question whose answer every heart knows: who is it that responds to the one in desperate need when he calls upon Him, removes the evil from him, and makes people successors on the earth, generation after generation? Is there any god besides Allah?
أَمَّنْ يُجِيبُ الْمُضْطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكْشِفُ السُّوءَ وَيَجْعَلُكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ الْأَرْضِ ۗ أَإِلَٰهٌ مَعَ اللَّهِ ۚ قَلِيلًا مَا تَذَكَّرُونَ

Desperation is a moment of truth in which the heart turns to Allah alone, which is why the verse promises: «He responds to the distressed when he calls upon Him». So when your situation becomes tight, do not hesitate to supplicate, be sincere in it, and stand at His door with your need just as it is.

The verse's ending, «little do you remember», draws attention to the fact that many people know their Lord in hardship and forget Him in ease. So keep your supplication present in both states, for whoever knows Allah in times of ease finds Him near in times of hardship.

en.title: A Transaction That Will Never Perish
en.excerpt: Recitation, prayer and spending in charity are a profitable trade that knows no loss.

body.text: The two verses describe those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer and spend secretly and openly as hoping for a trade that will neither stagnate nor lose; Allah will pay them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty. How profitable a trade it is!

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ وَأَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَأَنْفَقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً يَرْجُونَ تِجَارَةً لَنْ تَبُورَ
لِيُوَفِّيَهُمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَيَزِيدَهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ

Trade with people may profit or lose, but trade with Allah is always profitable, because He is «Forgiving and Appreciative»: He forgives shortcomings and appreciates the little. So give yourself a daily capital of these three: a page of the Qur'an, a prayer with humility, and a charity even if small. Then rejoice, for Allah will increase you from His bounty beyond what you hope.

en.title: And Do Not Forget Graciousness Between You
en.excerpt: Even at the time of parting, graciousness and kindness remain a character that is not forgotten.

body.text: The verse speaks about divorce before consummation, explains the obligatory right, then urges forgiveness, making it nearer to piety, and ends with a comprehensive instruction: that the two parties not forget graciousness between them.

وَإِن طَلَّقۡتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وَقَدۡ فَرَضۡتُمۡ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةٗ فَنِصۡفُ مَا فَرَضۡتُمۡ إِلَّآ أَن يَعۡفُونَ أَوۡ يَعۡفُوَاْ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِۦ عُقۡدَةُ ٱلنِّكَاحِۚ وَأَن تَعۡفُوٓاْ أَقۡرَبُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰۚ وَلَا تَنسَوُاْ ٱلۡفَضۡلَ بَيۡنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ

Relationships may end, but good character does not. The verse teaches us to part with dignity, not to deny a past kindness, and not to turn disagreement into hostility and public shaming. This principle applies to every family or social relationship: if you disagree with a relative or a partner, remember the good that was between you, and offer forgiveness, for it is nearer to piety.

en.title: The Reward of Allah Is Better
en.excerpt: When people wished for treasures like Qarun's, the people of knowledge reminded them that Allah's reward is better and more lasting.

body.text: Qarun comes out before his people in his adornment, dazzling the hearts of those who desire the life of this world and wish for the like of what he was given, while the people of knowledge stand to correct the scale and remind them of what is with Allah.

فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوْمِهِ فِي زِينَتِهِ ۖ قَالَ الَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا يَا لَيْتَ لَنَا مِثْلَ مَا أُوتِيَ قَارُونُ إِنَّهُ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ
وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ وَيْلَكُمْ ثَوَابُ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِمَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا وَلَا يُلَقَّاهَا إِلَّا الصَّابِرُونَ

Displays of luxury may dazzle the eyes and stir up longing, but beneficial knowledge rearranges values in the heart, so the believer knows that faith and righteous deeds are the greatest gain a person can attain. The verse ends by stating that this rank is granted to «none but the patient»: patience in not longing for what is in people's hands, and contentment with what Allah has apportioned, are the path to true happiness.

en.title: Whoever Believes in Allah, He Will Guide His Heart
en.excerpt: Whoever believes that calamity comes only by Allah's permission, Allah guides his heart to contentment and acceptance.

body.text: The verse affirms that no calamity strikes except by Allah's permission, then promises whoever believes in Allah a great reward in the midst of the trial: that Allah will guide his heart; and Allah has full knowledge of all things.
مَا أَصَابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ ۗ وَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ يَهْدِ قَلْبَهُ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

The guidance here is guidance for the heart in the moment of shock: that it settles, submits and is content, and sees in the calamity what others do not see of wisdom, reward and gentleness. This is guidance that a person cannot attain by himself; Allah grants it to whoever believes in Him.

So when a calamity befalls you, remember that it did not come outside of Allah's knowledge and permission, and ask Him to guide your heart, for a guided heart finds in hardship a serenity that lightens its burdens. And ask Allah for contentment and steadfastness in every trial.

en.title: The Home of the Hereafter Is Truly Life
en.excerpt: This world is diversion and play, while the Hereafter is the true, complete and everlasting life.

body.text: The verse compares two abodes: the life of this world, which is nothing but diversion and play that quickly passes, and the home of the Hereafter, which is true life, complete and everlasting, if only people truly knew.
وَمَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَآ إِلَّا لَهۡوٞ وَلَعِبٞۚ وَإِنَّ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ لَهِيَ ٱلۡحَيَوَانُۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ

The point is not to despise this world, but to put it in its proper size: it is a passage, and the Hereafter is the abode. His words «if only they knew» indicate that whoever knows the reality of the two abodes will not prefer what perishes over what endures. So ask yourself with every choice: which of the two abodes am I building with this?

en.title: So Make Peace Between Your Brothers
en.excerpt: Reconciling those in dispute is a fruit of the brotherhood of faith and a means to Allah's mercy.

body.text: The verse affirms that the believers are brothers, and builds a practical command upon that: making peace between those of them in dispute. It then links this to God-consciousness and the hope of mercy. Brotherhood is not a slogan, but a responsibility towards every disagreement that arises between brothers.
إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ

If you see estrangement between two friends or relatives, do not be a spectator, nor carry words between them and fan the flames. Rather, be gentle in bringing hearts together, pass on good words, and choose the right moment. Reconciliation is work that requires wisdom and patience, and its reward is mercy from Allah.

en.title: Adversity Has Touched Me, and You Are the Most Merciful of the Merciful
en.excerpt: Ayyub's supplication in his trial: a description of his state and praise of Allah, without resentment or objection.

body.text: After long illness and trial, Ayyub (peace be upon him) called upon his Lord with great courtesy: he mentioned the adversity that had afflicted him, then praised Allah as the Most Merciful of the merciful. So Allah answered him and removed the adversity he was in.
وَأَيُّوبَ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ

In illness and trial there is no harm in telling your Lord about your state, for He loves to see your brokenness before Him. But let your complaint be blended with praise of Him and good expectation of His mercy, for beautiful patience does not prevent supplication; rather, supplication is one of the greatest doors to relief.

en.title: Those Who Believe in the Unseen
en.excerpt: The first quality of the God-conscious is believing in what the eye cannot see of what Allah has informed us.

body.text: At the opening of Surah Al-Baqarah, the Qur'an is described as a Book in which there is no doubt, a guidance for the God-conscious. Then comes their first quality: they believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and spend from what Allah has provided them.

ذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيۡبَۛ فِيهِۛ هُدٗى لِّلۡمُتَّقِينَ
ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡغَيۡبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ

Faith in the unseen is the foundation on which everything after it is built. Whoever believes in meeting Allah, in Paradise and in the Fire without seeing them establishes prayer and spends with a tranquil heart. So strengthen this foundation by reflecting on what Allah has informed us of, and live as though you see what you have been promised.

Joining faith in the unseen with prayer and spending teaches you that true faith shows itself in deeds. So let every certainty in your heart have an effect on your day: a prayer you keep up, and spending even if little. It is the small, constant deeds that keep faith alive in the heart.

en.title: Say to My Servants Who Have Believed
en.excerpt: Establish your prayer and spend from your provision before a day comes when neither trade nor friendship will avail.

body.text: Allah commands His Prophet to tell His believing servants to establish prayer and spend secretly and openly, before a day comes in which there is no trading and no friendship. In attributing them to Himself with the words «My servants» there is honour and affection.
قُلْ لِعِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا يُقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَيُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ سِرًّا وَعَلَانِيَةً مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لَا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلَا خِلَالٌ

The opportunity is here now: you can pray, give charity and make up for what you missed, but on the Day of Resurrection no deed can be bought and worldly friendships will not avail. So hasten today and do not delay: a prayer you used to postpone, a charity you intended to give, or someone's right you kept putting off; for no one knows when the time for deeds will run out.

en.title: And Live with Them in Kindness
en.excerpt: Living together in kindness is a golden rule of married life, and a passing dislike may hide much good.

body.text: The verse forbids wronging women and harming them, or pressuring them to take back some of what they were given, and commands living with them in kindness. It then opens the door of hope: a person may dislike something while Allah places much good in it.

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَرِثُوا النِّسَاءَ كَرْهًا ۖ وَلَا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذْهَبُوا بِبَعْضِ مَا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ ۚ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ ۚ فَإِنْ كَرِهْتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰ أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيْرًا كَثِيرًا

Kindness (ma'ruf) is a comprehensive word: gentleness in speech, fairness in dealings, spending without reminding of favours, and patience with temperaments. It is what people recognise as good companionship. When the home goes through a period of coolness, do not judge the whole relationship by a moment of distress; the verse teaches you to look for the hidden good and to give the days a chance to reveal it.

en.title: They Were Youths Who Believed in Their Lord
en.excerpt: Young men who believed in their Lord, so Allah increased them in guidance; a sincere step is met with help from Allah.

body.text: Allah begins the detailed story of the People of the Cave with a brief description of its heroes: they were youths, young men in the prime of life, who believed in their Lord with sincere faith, and their reward was that Allah increased them in guidance and steadfastness.
نَّحۡنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيۡكَ نَبَأَهُم بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ إِنَّهُمۡ فِتۡيَةٌ ءَامَنُواْ بِرَبِّهِمۡ وَزِدۡنَٰهُمۡ هُدٗى

The verse honours believing youth, for youth is a stage of strength and enthusiasm, and when it is directed towards faith it becomes one of the greatest causes of good. These young men held firm to the truth in an environment that did not help them. His words «and We increased them in guidance» show a divine law: whoever takes a sincere step towards Allah, Allah increases him in success and guidance. So do not belittle your beginnings in obedience, for guidance grows with sincerity and perseverance.

en.title: There Is No God but He, So Take Him as Guardian
en.excerpt: Devoting oneself to Allah through remembrance and worship gives rise to true reliance on Him in all matters.

body.text: The two verses command remembering the name of Allah and devoting oneself to Him sincerely, then mention that He is the Lord of the East and the West, there is no god but He, and build a clear conclusion on that: «so take Him as Guardian».

وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا
رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا

Reliance is a fruit of knowledge and worship. Whoever knows that Allah is the Lord of all directions and that there is none worthy of worship besides Him will naturally rely on Him alone and not attach his heart to a created being like himself. Affirming Allah's oneness is the foundation of tranquility.

Set aside a quiet time for remembrance in which you cut yourself off from distractions, for this brief withdrawal rearranges the heart and lets you go out to people carrying a lighter load, because you have handed your affairs to a capable Guardian. How happy is the one who finds this rest!

en.title: To Test You as to Which of You Is Best in Deed
en.excerpt: Death and life were created as a test, and the measure is the excellence of deeds, not their quantity.

body.text: The verse tells us that Allah created death and life to test His servants as to which of them is best in deed, and then ends with two noble names: the Almighty, the Forgiving; might that cannot be overcome, and vast forgiveness for whoever returns to Him and repents.
ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلۡمَوۡتَ وَٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ لِيَبۡلُوَكُمۡ أَيُّكُمۡ أَحۡسَنُ عَمَلٗاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ

The verse did not say «which of you does the most», but «which of you is best in deed». What matters is excellence: that the deed be sincere, correct and well done. So do not exhaust yourself with quantity without spirit; perfect a little and keep it up. And mentioning death before life reminds you that the end is ever present, so you live with a prepared heart.

en.title: And Speak Good to People
en.excerpt: A good word is the right of all people, not only of those we love.

body.text: In the context of the covenant Allah took from the Children of Israel came the command to be good to parents, relatives, orphans and the needy, and along with it a general command: «And speak good to people». Good speech is not reserved for one group over another.

وَإِذۡ أَخَذۡنَا مِيثَٰقَ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ لَا تَعۡبُدُونَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَانٗا وَذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسۡنٗا وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُواْ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيۡتُمۡ إِلَّا قَلِيلٗا مِّنكُمۡ وَأَنتُم مُّعۡرِضُونَ

Keep your tongue gentle with everyone: with the shopkeeper, the worker, the neighbour, and the one who disagrees with you. A good word costs you nothing, yet it may open a closed heart or extinguish anger. And if you must give advice or criticism, offer it in the best words and the gentlest manner.
