en.title: My Lord, I Seek Refuge in You from the Incitements of the Devils
en.excerpt: Seeking refuge in Allah is the believer's fortress against the whispers, promptings and presence of Satan.

body.text: Allah teaches His Prophet ﷺ to seek refuge in Him from the incitements of the devils, that is, their whispers and goading that drive one to anger and evil, and to seek refuge in Him from their being present in any of his affairs.

وَقُل رَّبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزَٰتِ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِ
وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّ أَن يَحْضُرُونِ

Satan creeps in on you in moments of anger and heedlessness, and seeking refuge in Allah is the first weapon. If you feel anger rising or a whisper inviting you to evil, turn to your Lord with these words, and ask Him to keep the devils away from your prayer, your home and all your affairs.

en.title: He Is with Them Wherever They Are
en.excerpt: No two or three gather for a private conversation but Allah knows it; so watch over your gatherings.

body.text: The verse affirms the vastness of Allah's knowledge of what is in the heavens and the earth: there is no private conversation among three but He is the fourth of them by His knowledge, nor among five but He is the sixth of them, and then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection.

أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۖ مَا يَكُونُ مِنْ نَجْوَىٰ ثَلَاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ وَلَا خَمْسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سَادِسُهُمْ وَلَا أَدْنَىٰ مِنْ ذَٰلِكَ وَلَا أَكْثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كَانُوا ۖ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا عَمِلُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

If you keep this verse in mind in your gatherings, your conversation will change: no backbiting, no scheming, and no word that hurts anyone, because Allah is «with them wherever they are» by His knowledge. So fill your gatherings with your companions with good, even if they are private and far from people's eyes.

The verse also brings comfort to the believer: when you gather with your brothers for an act of obedience, advice or reconciliation, know that Allah knows and sees it, and will inform you of it on the Day of Resurrection, so that it is a witness for you, not against you.

en.title: My Lord, Make Me an Establisher of Prayer, and from My Descendants
en.excerpt: Steadfastness in prayer is a blessing to be sought from Allah through supplication, for oneself and one's children.

body.text: This is the supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), the intimate friend of the Most Merciful, asking his Lord to make him and his descendants establishers of prayer. Despite his lofty rank, he did not rely on himself, but sought success from Allah.
رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي ۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ

Herein is a lesson for every Muslim: keeping up the prayer is a gift of success from Allah before it is an effort of yours, so ask Him for steadfastness in it as you ask Him for provision and well-being. And do not forget your children in this supplication; make it a regular supplication in your prostration, while striving to be a good example for them in hastening to prayer, and then conclude as he concluded: «and accept my supplication».

en.title: If They Both Desire Reconciliation, Allah Will Bring About Harmony Between Them
en.excerpt: A sincere will to reconcile is the key to Allah bringing a couple together.

body.text: When a rift between spouses is feared, the verse guides to sending an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from hers, and then promises that if they both desire reconciliation, Allah will bring about harmony between the spouses.
وَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ شِقَاقَ بَيْنِهِمَا فَابْعَثُوا حَكَمًا مِنْ أَهْلِهِ وَحَكَمًا مِنْ أَهْلِهَا إِنْ يُرِيدَا إِصْلَاحًا يُوَفِّقِ اللَّهُ بَيْنَهُمَا ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا خَبِيرًا

In this verse, the families are part of the solution, not part of the problem: their role is to put out the disagreement wisely, not to take sides and inflame it. The divine promise is conditional on sincere intention: whoever enters into reconciliation wanting good, Allah grants him success even if the matter seems difficult. So if you are a party to a dispute, begin by correcting your intention before searching for arguments.

en.title: I Will Not Stretch Out My Hand Against You
en.excerpt: One of the two sons of Adam meets a threat of murder with fear of Allah, and reminds that acceptance is for the God-conscious.

body.text: The two sons of Adam each offer a sacrifice. It is accepted from one of them and not from the other, so envy flares up in the heart of the second and he threatens his brother with murder. His brother answers him with words overflowing with piety and wisdom.

وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ابْنَيْ آدَمَ بِالْحَقِّ إِذْ قَرَّبَا قُرْبَانًا فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ الْآخَرِ قَالَ لَأَقْتُلَنَّكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ
لَئِنْ بَسَطْتَ إِلَيَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقْتُلَنِي مَا أَنَا بِبَاسِطٍ يَدِيَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ ۖ إِنِّي أَخَافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ

Envy begins as a feeling in the heart and may then lead to the greatest of crimes. Its cure is for the servant to busy himself with reforming himself, for «Allah only accepts from the God-conscious», not from one who envies others for Allah's bounty. The righteous brother's stance holds a lesson in self-restraint: nothing prevented him from repaying evil with evil except his fear of Allah. The believer does not make other people's actions the measure of his own; he makes fear of Allah the judge.

en.title: Let Man Look at His Food
en.excerpt: Behind every morsel is a journey of water, earth and plants, all of it by Allah's arrangement.

body.text: The verses invite man to reflect on the food he eats every day: how Allah poured down water from the sky in abundance, then split the earth open so that the plants on which he lives might come forth from it.

فَلۡيَنظُرِ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِهِۦٓ
أَنَّا صَبَبۡنَا ٱلۡمَآءَ صَبّٗا
ثُمَّ شَقَقۡنَا ٱلۡأَرۡضَ شَقّٗا

The morsel we take in a moment has passed through long stages over which we have no control: rain that falls, earth that splits, a seed that sprouts. This reflection turns eating from a heedless habit into an act of grateful worship. How many blessings pass us by while we are unaware of them!

At your next meal, try pausing for a moment before you begin to recall this journey, then mention Allah's name and praise Him afterwards. And avoid waste, for what has reached you through such arrangement should not be squandered.

en.title: Whoever Does an Atom's Weight of Good Will See It
en.excerpt: No good deed is lost with Allah, even if it is an atom's weight, and no evil is overlooked, however small.

body.text: Two comprehensive verses on the scale of recompense: whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it. Nothing is lost with Allah, and nothing is forgotten, however minute and small.

فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ
وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ

This verse gives value to every moment: a sincere smile, removing something harmful from the road, a good word; you will see them all. Likewise the hurtful word and the forbidden glance. So do not wait for great deeds before you begin; the path to Allah is paved with small atoms of good that accumulate day after day until they make the scale heavy.

en.title: And Be with the Truthful
en.excerpt: Truthfulness is acquired through companionship, so be with the truthful and you will become one of them.

body.text: The verse joins the command to be God-conscious with the command to be with the truthful. Truthfulness is not a passing word but a way of life that is strengthened by accompanying its people and following their example in their words, deeds and intentions.
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَكُونُوا مَعَ الصَّادِقِينَ

A person is influenced by those he sits with. If you want to be truthful, draw close to people of truthfulness, read their biographies, and keep away from environments of false flattery and exaggeration. And begin with yourself: do not lie even in jest, do not embellish facts, and be truthful with Allah in your intention before being truthful with people in your speech.

en.title: Grant Us from Our Spouses and Offspring Comfort to Our Eyes
en.excerpt: Among the qualities of the servants of the Most Merciful is that they ask Allah to make their homes righteous and to make them examples for the God-conscious.

body.text: At the close of the description of the servants of the Most Merciful, Allah mentions their supplication that He grant them from their spouses and offspring what will comfort their eyes in righteousness and obedience, and that He make them leaders to be followed in goodness.
وَٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبۡ لَنَا مِنۡ أَزۡوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعۡيُنٖ وَٱجۡعَلۡنَا لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا

A righteous home is a great blessing to be sought from Allah through supplication along with good upbringing and treatment. So pray for your spouse and your children to be guided, and strive to be an example of goodness for them yourself, for a person does not become a leader of the God-conscious until he begins by reforming himself.

en.title: Does He Not Know, He Who Created?
en.excerpt: The One who made you knows you better than you know yourself; so trust His arrangement even when its wisdom is hidden from you.

body.text: A question that affirms a self-evident truth: does the Creator not know His creation, their secrets and what is even more hidden than a secret? It then ends with two majestic names: the Subtle, gentle with His servants, and the All-Aware of their affairs. It is a verse that combines affirming His knowledge with a reminder of His mercy.
أَلَا يَعۡلَمُ مَنۡ خَلَقَ وَهُوَ ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ

If you do not know the wisdom in a decree that has befallen you, remember that the One who created you knows best what is good for you; the maker knows his work best. So do not object to what you do not understand; be content, ask Allah for good, and know that He is «the Subtle, the All-Aware».

The name the Subtle (al-Latif) means that He brings good to you through hidden ways you do not expect, and the All-Aware (al-Khabir) means that He knows the finest details of your affairs. So combine reassurance in His gentleness with mindfulness of His knowledge. Do not despair of His gentleness, nor be heedless of His watchfulness, for He knows the secret and what is even more hidden.

en.title: So Glory Be to Allah When You Reach Evening
en.excerpt: Glorifying Allah at the ends of the day keeps the whole day connected to Him.

body.text: These two verses call us to glorify and praise Allah at different times: in the evening and the morning, in the late afternoon and at midday. It is as if the whole day were surrounded by the remembrance of Allah from beginning to end.

فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وَحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ
وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَعَشِيًّا وَحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ

So do not confine the remembrance of Allah to a single time; spread it over your day: the morning remembrances, glorification on the road, praise at every blessing, and the evening remembrances before night falls. And remember that to Him belongs «all praise in the heavens and the earth»: the whole universe praises Him, and when your tongue joins this praise you are in harmony with the existence around you.

en.title: And Speak to Them Words of Kindness
en.excerpt: When dividing an inheritance, do not forget the needy relative and the orphan, even if only with a kind word.

body.text: The verse guides the heirs, when relatives who do not inherit, orphans or the needy are present at the division, to give them something of the wealth and to speak to them words of kindness that console their hearts.
وَإِذَا حَضَرَ الْقِسْمَةَ أُولُو الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينُ فَارْزُقُوهُمْ مِنْهُ وَقُولُوا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفًا

The moment of division can be a moment of tension among relatives, and the verse turns it into an occasion for generosity and consoling hearts, so that no one leaves it brokenhearted. Combining giving with kind words holds a lesson: a good word is part of kindness, and giving without gentleness loses much of its effect.

en.title: This Is a Mercy from My Lord
en.excerpt: Dhul-Qarnayn completed a great work, then attributed all the credit to his Lord's mercy.

body.text: After Dhul-Qarnayn finished building the great barrier with which he protected the weak people, he did not attribute the achievement to his strength or expertise; rather, he said that it was a mercy from his Lord, and reminded them that every structure in this world has an appointed end.
قَالَ هَٰذَا رَحۡمَةٞ مِّن رَّبِّيۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعۡدُ رَبِّي جَعَلَهُۥ دَكَّآءَۖ وَكَانَ وَعۡدُ رَبِّي حَقّٗا

True achievement does not make its owner forget Allah's favour. Dhul-Qarnayn, with all the dominion and power he had been given, attributed his work to Allah's mercy, and this is one of the greatest signs of humility and sincere faith in success. In his words «He will make it level with the ground» is a reminder that whatever man builds, however solid, will pass away by Allah's command. So let us work and do it well, but not cling to our works in a way that makes us forget that what endures is the Face of Allah and whatever was done for His sake.

en.title: Do They Not Look at the Camels, How They Were Created?
en.excerpt: A Qur'anic call to look reflectively at the creatures around us, both near and far.

body.text: The verses pose a question that urges looking: at the camels, how they were created; at the sky, how it was raised; and at the mountains, how they were set firm. These were scenes before the eyes of those addressed every day.

أَفَلَا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ
وَإِلَى السَّمَاءِ كَيْفَ رُفِعَتْ
وَإِلَى الْجِبَالِ كَيْفَ نُصِبَتْ

The Qur'an here does not ask for mere seeing with the eye, but for reflective looking that asks about the how and the why: how was this creature suited to its environment? How was the sky raised without pillars that we see? How were the mountains made firm? Looking becomes worship when it is joined with reflection.

So take your immediate surroundings as a school of faith: an animal you see, a sky above you, or a mountain on your way. Whenever you ask «how» with a present heart, the question will lead you to the greatness of the Creator. The universe is an open book for whoever wishes to read.

en.title: Competition in Increase Diverts You
en.excerpt: Competing in accumulation distracts the heart from its purpose until its owner reaches the grave.

body.text: The surah opens with an address that awakens the heedless: boasting about abundance of wealth, children and followers has distracted you from obeying Allah and preparing to meet Him, until you reached the graves and your lives ended while you were still in that race.

أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ
حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ

Competition in increase has no limit: whenever a person attains something he seeks more, and a lifetime may pass in the race. The expression «until you visit the graves» likens remaining in the grave to a visit, hinting that a resurrection lies beyond it. So review what occupies your time and your thoughts: is it something you need, or merely comparison with what others have?

en.title: Take What Is Given Freely and Enjoin What Is Good
en.excerpt: A single verse that contains a complete method for dealing with people.

body.text: The verse gathers three instructions for dealing with people: accept from them what comes easily of their character and do not scrutinise them exhaustively, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant without answering their foolishness in kind.
خُذِ ٱلْعَفْوَ وَأْمُرْ بِٱلْعُرْفِ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ

Do not demand perfection from people; accept what they can easily give and overlook their shortcomings, for nitpicking ruins relationships. Yet do not stay silent about good; call to it gently. And if an ignorant person confronts you with foolishness, turn away from him, for turning away here is strength and wisdom, not weakness.

en.title: My Lord, Enable Me to Be Grateful for Your Favour
en.excerpt: Sulayman hears the ant's words and smiles, then asks Allah to enable him to be grateful for His blessings.

body.text: When Sulayman (peace be upon him) heard the ant warning her community, he smiled, amused, and remembered Allah's blessing upon him in granting him this knowledge. So he asked his Lord to inspire him to be grateful for His favour upon him and upon his parents, and to enable him to do righteous deeds that please Him.

فَتَبَسَّمَ ضَاحِكًا مِنْ قَوْلِهَا وَقَالَ رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَالِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحًا تَرْضَاهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِي عِبَادِكَ الصَّالِحِينَ

Gratitude itself is a blessing that requires divine help, which is why Sulayman asked his Lord for it. Whenever you see a blessing in yourself or your family, ask Allah to help you be grateful for it, remember His blessings upon your parents too, and then make gratitude a righteous deed, not merely words.

en.title: You Are the Ones in Need of Allah
en.excerpt: Your need for Allah is not a shameful weakness, but a truth that, once you know it, makes you the richest of people.

body.text: An address to all people that affirms the reality of their existence: you are the ones in need of Allah in all your affairs and conditions, and Allah is Free of need of you, Praiseworthy in all that He decrees. This address is a reminder of a truth that man often forgets.
يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنْتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ ۖ وَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ

The words «you are the ones in need» include the rich, the strong and the learned; no one can do without his Lord for a single breath or morsel. So if you feel self-sufficient, remember this verse, and if you feel helpless, let it drive you to supplication, not to despair.

Whoever knows his need for Allah becomes free of need of people: he does not humble himself before any created being, nor does his heart attach itself to anyone's gift. He takes from the means as much as he needs while his heart is turned towards «the Free of need, the Praiseworthy». This is the true honour the believer finds.

en.title: My Prayer, My Sacrifice, My Living and My Dying Are for Allah
en.excerpt: When the whole of life is for Allah, every moment in it becomes worship.

body.text: These two verses proclaim the meaning of sincerity in its widest form: not only prayer and sacrifice are for Allah, but all of life and death as well, so that nothing in the believer's lifetime remains outside the pleasure of his Lord.

قُلۡ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحۡيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُۥۖ وَبِذَٰلِكَ أُمِرۡتُ وَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ

With this intention, ordinary activity becomes an act of drawing near: your sleep to gain strength for obedience, your work to provide for yourself and your family, your food to carry out what Allah commanded you; all of it is recorded on your scale. So renew your intention at the start of your day, and let your motto be «He has no partner». Sincerity is what makes a small deed great, and protects worship from being shared with the ego's desires.

en.title: Or Reconciliation Between People
en.excerpt: Most private talk holds no good, except what is charity, kindness or reconciliation.

body.text: The verse affirms that there is no good in much of what people converse about privately, except for one who enjoins charity, kindness or reconciliation between people, and it promises whoever does so seeking the pleasure of Allah a great reward.

لَا خَيْرَ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِنْ نَجْوَاهُمْ إِلَّا مَنْ أَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ أَوْ مَعْرُوفٍ أَوْ إِصْلَاحٍ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ ۚ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاتِ اللَّهِ فَسَوْفَ نُؤْتِيهِ أَجْرًا عَظِيمًا

Our family gatherings and side conversations may be full of complaint and criticism, and the verse invites us to make them gatherings of good: suggesting help for someone in need, or working towards reconciling those in dispute. The condition of seeking Allah's pleasure protects the one striving from showing off; so let your peacemaking among your family be for Allah, not to be praised for wisdom or to win one side over.

en.title: Had He Not Been of Those Who Glorify Allah
en.excerpt: Yunus's remembrance of his Lord was a cause of his rescue; remembrance in times of ease is a store for times of hardship.

body.text: The two verses tell us that had Yunus (peace be upon him) not been among those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in the belly of the whale until the Day of Resurrection. His glorification was a cause of his rescue from those darknesses.

فَلَوْلَا أَنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الْمُسَبِّحِينَ
لَلَبِثَ فِي بَطْنِهِ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ

The righteous deeds a servant keeps up become a reserve for him in hardships. Whoever knows Allah in times of ease through remembrance and obedience will find that among the greatest causes of relief from his distress in times of trial. So keep a fixed portion of glorification and remembrance, even if small, for a little that is constant builds a bond between you and your Lord, and it is this bond that benefits you when all means are cut off.

en.title: And Do Not Despair of Relief from Allah
en.excerpt: However long the loss, the door to relief is open, and despairing of Allah's mercy is not among the qualities of believers.

body.text: After years of loss and pain, a patient father directs his sons to go out and search, and pairs this with a great instruction: «and do not despair», for despairing of Allah's relief is not the way of the people of faith.
يَا بَنِيَّ اذْهَبُوا فَتَحَسَّسُوا مِنْ يُوسُفَ وَأَخِيهِ وَلَا تَيْأَسُوا مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّهُ لَا يَيْأَسُ مِنْ رَوْحِ اللَّهِ إِلَّا الْقَوْمُ الْكَافِرُونَ

The verse combines two things: acting on the means, «Go and search diligently», and heartfelt hope in Allah's relief. True hope is not lazy waiting; it is striving with certainty that Allah is able to change the situation. So combine effort and hope, and do not separate them.

If something you are waiting for takes a long time, do not let despair creep into your heart. Keep trying, and think well of your Lord, for Allah's relief and mercy are nearer than you think. Despair makes a person sit idle, while hope drives him to action.

en.title: And Restrained the Soul from Its Desires
en.excerpt: Fearing the standing before Allah and restraining the soul from its desires is a path to Paradise, the refuge.

body.text: The two verses mention two qualities of the people of Paradise: they feared the standing before their Lord, that is, standing before Him for the reckoning, and they restrained their souls from desires and the sins they incline towards. So Paradise became their refuge and dwelling.

وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِۦ وَنَهَى ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ
فَإِنَّ ٱلْجَنَّةَ هِىَ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ

The soul inclines towards what it craves, and struggling against it is not a one-time effort but daily work. The verse gives you the key to that struggle: keeping in mind your standing before Allah. When your soul calls you to what does not please Him, remember that standing, and say to it: I will not give you everything you crave, for true rest lies in the refuge Allah has promised.

en.title: We Feed You Only for the Sake of Allah
en.excerpt: The most beautiful giving is that which is free of waiting for thanks or anything in return.

body.text: The two verses describe the righteous as those who give food, despite their love for it and their own need of it, to the needy, the orphan and the captive, and then declare their intention: we want from you neither reward nor thanks; we feed you only for the sake of Allah.

وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا
إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنْكُمْ جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا

Watch your intention when you give: are you waiting for a word of thanks? Are you upset if your kindness is not mentioned? Freeing your giving from expecting a return brings rest to the heart and makes kindness purely for Allah. So give and then forget, and leave the reward to the One with whom nothing is ever lost.

en.title: Our Lord, We Have Believed, So Forgive Us Our Sins
en.excerpt: The God-conscious approach their Lord through their faith, then ask Him for forgiveness and salvation from the Fire.

body.text: The verse describes the state of the God-conscious, for whom Allah has prepared gardens, and mentions among their words this supplication: they affirm before their Lord that they have believed, then ask Him to forgive them their sins and protect them from the punishment of the Fire.
الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا آمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ

Faith is the greatest means by which a servant approaches his Lord, for it is a righteous deed that Allah loves. So when you supplicate, put before your request your affirmation of faith and of Allah's oneness, then ask for forgiveness and salvation. And do not be deluded by your faith, for the God-conscious themselves sought pardon and feared the Fire despite their righteousness.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 16

en.title: None Can Remove It Except Him
en.excerpt: Both harm and good are in Allah's hand; so the heart turns to Him alone in both states.

body.text: The verse affirms that whatever harm befalls a person, none can remove it but Allah, and whatever good befalls him, none can repel it, for He has power over all things and nothing is beyond Him.
وَإِن يَمۡسَسۡكَ ٱللَّهُ بِضُرّٖ فَلَا كَاشِفَ لَهُۥٓ إِلَّا هُوَۖ وَإِن يَمۡسَسۡكَ بِخَيۡرٖ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٞ

In illness and hardship people turn to the means, which is legitimate, but the verse reminds us that the true Remover of harm is Allah: «none can remove it». So combine medicine and supplication, and keep your heart attached to the Healer, not to the means.

And when good touches you, do not attribute it to your cleverness alone; thank Allah for it. Remembering the source of a blessing preserves it, and keeps your heart humble in ease just as it is beseeching in hardship. In this way your heart stays connected to your Lord in all your states.

en.title: Indeed, Good Deeds Remove Evil Deeds
en.excerpt: Prayer at the ends of the day erases the slips that have clung to the heart.

body.text: This verse commands establishing prayer at the two ends of the day and in hours of the night, and then gives the reason with a heartening principle: good deeds remove evil deeds. Prayers are stations at which the servant is purified of what befalls him during his day.
وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ وَزُلَفًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ ۚ إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ذِكْرَىٰ لِلذَّاكِرِينَ

So do not despair if your foot slips during the day; make the next prayer a new beginning. Stand in it with a humbled heart and follow it with whatever good deeds you can, for a good deed erases a bad one by Allah's grace. The verse ends by stating that this is «a reminder for those who remember»; whoever remembers Allah much finds in this meaning both comfort and motivation.

en.title: And Cooperate in Righteousness and Piety
en.excerpt: A strong society is built on cooperation in good and on restraining one another from sin and aggression.

body.text: In the context of rulings about the Sacred Precinct and the rites, the verse lays down a general social principle: cooperate in righteousness and piety, do not cooperate in sin and aggression, and do not let hatred of a people drive you to transgress against them.

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُحِلُّوا شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ وَلَا الشَّهْرَ الْحَرَامَ وَلَا الْهَدْيَ وَلَا الْقَلَائِدَ وَلَا آمِّينَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرَامَ يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَرِضْوَانًا ۚ وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطَادُوا ۚ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ أَنْ تَعْتَدُوا ۘ وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۖ إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ

Cooperation at home begins with sharing burdens, and in the neighbourhood with small initiatives: sponsoring someone, cleaning a mosque, or helping a sick person. All of this is part of the righteousness we were commanded to cooperate in. The other side of the principle is no less important: that we do not help anyone in wrongdoing, even a relative or friend; true support is to hold him back from his mistake.

en.title: They Used to Hasten to Good Deeds
en.excerpt: The household of Zakariya is an example of a righteous family: hastening to good, supplicating in hope and fear, and humility before Allah.

body.text: After Allah answered Zakariya (peace be upon him), granting him Yahya and making his wife fit for him, the verse mentions the qualities of this blessed family that were a cause of this gift, in three comprehensive traits.
فَٱسۡتَجَبۡنَا لَهُۥ وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُۥ يَحۡيَىٰ وَأَصۡلَحۡنَا لَهُۥ زَوۡجَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِي ٱلۡخَيۡرَٰتِ وَيَدۡعُونَنَا رَغَبٗا وَرَهَبٗاۖ وَكَانُواْ لَنَا خَٰشِعِينَ

The verse did not mention abundant wealth or high status; it mentioned three qualities: hastening to good deeds, supplicating in hope and fear, and humility before Allah. These are the qualities that make a home blessed and a supplication answered.

So make hastening to good a habit in your home: in prayer, charity, keeping family ties and helping the needy. Teach your family to call upon Allah hoping for His mercy and fearing His punishment, so that hope and awe come together in the heart.

en.title: So Look at the Effects of Allah's Mercy
en.excerpt: The effects of Allah's mercy are around us in every land that turns green after drought, and they are proof of His power to resurrect.

body.text: The verse commands looking at the effects of Allah's mercy: how He revives the earth after its death with rain and vegetation. It then concludes that the One who does this is able to give life to the dead, and He has power over all things.
فَانْظُرْ إِلَىٰ آثَارِ رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْيِي الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا ۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمُحْيِي الْمَوْتَىٰ ۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

Rain is called here an effect of mercy, which teaches us to read events with the eye of mercy rather than the eye of habit. Every green shoot after dryness is a message that Allah does not forget His servants. Mercy surrounds us on every side.

When you go through a period of drought in provision, health or a relationship, look at the earth that was dead and then turned green, and remember that the Allah who did that is able to change your situation for the better.

en.title: While Their Hearts Are Fearful
en.excerpt: The believer does righteous deeds and fears they may not be accepted, and this fear drives him to hasten.

body.text: The two verses describe people who perform acts of obedience and give generously, yet their hearts are fearful that it may not be accepted from them, because they are certain they will return to their Lord. It is they who hasten to good deeds and are foremost in them.

وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْتُونَ مَآ ءَاتَوا۟ وَّقُلُوبُهُمْ وَجِلَةٌ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ رَٰجِعُونَ
أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ يُسَٰرِعُونَ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ وَهُمْ لَهَا سَٰبِقُونَ

This fear is not an anxiety that paralyses its owner, but an awe that protects him from vanity and being deluded by his deeds. That is why the verse follows it with hastening to good deeds: one who fears non-acceptance does more and does not stop. So when you perform an act of obedience, do not look at it with admiration; ask Allah to accept it, and move on to another act of obedience after it.

en.title: As for the Orphan, Do Not Oppress Him
en.excerpt: Gentleness with the orphan and the one who asks is practical gratitude for Allah's blessing upon you.

body.text: After the surah reminded of Allah's blessings, the practical instruction came: do not oppress or humiliate the orphan, and do not repel or rebuke the one who asks. Gratitude for a blessing shows itself in mercy towards those weaker than you.

فَأَمَّا ٱلۡيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقۡهَرۡ
وَأَمَّا ٱلسَّآئِلَ فَلَا تَنۡهَرۡ

You may not always have something to give the one who asks, but you can always turn him away gently. You may not be able to sponsor an orphan, but you can honour him with a word and a smile. Mercy towards the weak begins with good treatment before money, and with respecting their dignity before meeting their need.

en.title: Seek Forgiveness of Your Lord; Indeed, He Is Ever Forgiving
en.excerpt: Seeking forgiveness is not only a cause for sins to be forgiven, but a door to rain, provision and offspring.

body.text: Nuh (peace be upon him) relates what he called his people to: that they seek forgiveness of their Lord, the Ever-Forgiving, and he promised them that Allah would send rain upon them in abundance, provide them with wealth and children, and give them gardens and rivers.

فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ غَفَّارًا
يُرْسِلِ السَّمَاءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْرَارًا
وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ أَنْهَارًا

If your provision is tight or what you hope for is delayed, seek forgiveness abundantly while taking the means. The verses link returning to Allah with blessing in rain, wealth and children. Keep a daily portion of seeking forgiveness, and trust that your Lord is Ever-Forgiving and Generous.

en.title: Be, and It Is
en.excerpt: What seems impossible in your calculations, a single word from Allah brings into being.

body.text: Surah Ya-Sin closes by explaining the perfection of Allah's power: when He wills a thing, He says to it «Be», and it is. Then He is declared free of all imperfection, for in His hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him people will be returned.

إِنَّمَآ أَمۡرُهُۥٓ إِذَآ أَرَادَ شَيۡـًٔا أَن يَقُولَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
فَسُبۡحَٰنَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِۦ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ

A need may stay with you so long that you think it remote, but the verse reminds you that with Allah the matter is «Be, and it is». So do not judge your supplication by the measure of the means alone; supplicate with certainty, and take whatever steps you can.

In His words «in whose hand is the dominion of all things» there is rest for one exhausted by managing his affairs: you manage what concerns you and leave what you do not control to the One in whose hand is everything. Then you remember «and to Him you will be returned», and you work for that day. Thus hope and action come together for you.

en.title: Enjoin Prayer upon Your Family and Be Steadfast in It
en.excerpt: Establishing prayer in the home requires long patience, and its outcome is good.

body.text: This verse commands two inseparable things: that you enjoin prayer upon your family, and that you yourself be steadfast in it. Calling to good begins at home, example comes before words, and the road requires endurance.
وَأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلَاةِ وَاصْطَبِرْ عَلَيْهَا ۖ لَا نَسْأَلُكَ رِزْقًا ۖ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكَ ۗ وَالْعَاقِبَةُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ

The form «and be steadfast» indicates a redoubled and continuous patience. So do not despair if your children are late or lazy; repeat the reminder gently, pray in front of them, and give prayer a beloved presence in your home. The verse also offers reassurance: «We provide for you», so do not let worry about provision distract you from prayer, for provision is guaranteed, and the good outcome belongs to the God-conscious.

en.title: They Are Allies of One Another
en.excerpt: Believing men and women are one body: they support one another, advise one another and share in obedience.

body.text: The verse describes the believing men and women as allies of one another: they support and love one another, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, establish prayer and give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. It then promises them that Allah will have mercy on them.

وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتُ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ ۚ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَيُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَيُطِيعُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ سَيَرْحَمُهُمُ اللَّهُ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ

Alliance here means love, support and shared responsibility. Men and women in the believing society are partners in good, each helping the other in obedience. This begins at home: a couple who cooperate in prayer and charity and advise each other gently, so that their home becomes the nucleus of a cohesive society upon which mercy descends.

en.title: And Do Good as Allah Has Done Good to You
en.excerpt: The advice Qarun's people gave him is a balanced approach to wealth: a Hereafter not forgotten, and a worldly life not neglected.

body.text: The righteous among the people of Musa advise Qarun, who had been deluded by his treasures. They set before him a balanced scale for dealing with wealth, one that combines seeking the Hereafter, enjoying what is permissible, doing good, and avoiding corruption.

وَابْتَغِ فِيمَا آتَاكَ اللَّهُ الدَّارَ الْآخِرَةَ ۖ وَلَا تَنْسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَأَحْسِنْ كَمَا أَحْسَنَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ ۖ وَلَا تَبْغِ الْفَسَادَ فِي الْأَرْضِ ۖ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ

The advice did not ask him to abandon the world entirely; rather it said, “and do not forget your share,” even though the great goal is “the home of the Hereafter.” Islam does not forbid good things, but it makes wealth a means to Allah's pleasure. And the words “do good as [Allah] has done good” are a beautiful principle: whenever you remember Allah's goodness to you in your provision and health, meet it with goodness to people. A blessing whose benefit never reaches beyond its owner may turn into a trial.

en.title: With Him Are the Keys of the Unseen
en.excerpt: Allah's knowledge encompasses every falling leaf and every hidden grain, so how could the state of His servant escape Him?

body.text: The verse paints an awe-inspiring picture of how Allah's knowledge encompasses all things: with Him are the keys of the unseen, which none knows but He. He knows what is on land and in the sea; not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darkness of the earth.

وَعِندَهُۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةٖ فِي ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبٖ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبٖ مُّبِينٖ

If Allah knows the small leaf as it falls, and the grain buried in the darkness of the soil, how could the worry you hide or the prayer you whisper escape Him? He knows your state better than you do, and He is more merciful to you than you are to yourself.

This meaning gives the heart a wondrous tranquility: you are neither forgotten nor hidden, and the unknown that worries you is in the hand of the One who holds its keys. So entrust the future to Him, and occupy yourself with what you have been commanded in the present. And think well of Him.

en.title: Let Every Soul Look to What It Has Sent Forth for Tomorrow
en.excerpt: Take yourself to account today: what have you sent forth for the tomorrow that awaits you with Allah?

body.text: The verse commands the believers to be mindful of Allah, and that every soul should look to what it has sent forth for tomorrow. Then it warns against the state of those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves, and they did not work for what would benefit and save them.

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْتَنْظُرْ نَفْسٌ مَا قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ ۖ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ نَسُوا اللَّهَ فَأَنْسَاهُمْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ

Allah called the Day of Resurrection “tomorrow” to make you feel how near it is: “what it has sent forth for tomorrow.” Taking yourself to account is a simple daily habit: a few minutes before sleep in which you ask, what did I offer today, and what did I waste? Whoever forgets his Lord forgets his own true interest, even if he thinks he is serving it; it is the remembrance of Allah that keeps your soul safe for you.

en.title: Those Who Are Faithful to Their Trusts and Promises
en.excerpt: Faithfully keeping trusts and promises is a constant trait of the people of faith.

body.text: Among the qualities of the believers whom Allah exempted from anxious impatience, the verse mentions that they tend to their trusts and their promises. Tending is more than mere fulfilment: it is constant safekeeping, follow-up and care, as a shepherd tends what he has been entrusted with.
وَٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ لِأَمَٰنَٰتِهِمْ وَعَهْدِهِمْ رَٰعُونَ

So be a guardian of your trusts, not merely a carrier of them: check on whatever has been entrusted to you, whether money, a secret or a responsibility, and look after it with care and excellence. Keep your promises to people present in your mind, and do not wait for the other person to remind you of them.

en.title: Remember Allah with Much Remembrance
en.excerpt: Abundant remembrance and glorification morning and evening is a command for every believer, not for devout worshippers alone.

body.text: Allah addresses all the believers, telling them to remember Him abundantly, not limited to a particular time, place or situation, and to glorify Him and declare Him free of every imperfection at the beginning and end of the day, so that their whole day is surrounded by His remembrance from start to finish.

يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ ذِكۡرٗا كَثِيرٗا
وَسَبِّحُوهُ بُكۡرَةٗ وَأَصِيلًا

No fixed amount of remembrance was required, only abundance, because it is an easy act of worship available in every situation: on the road, at work and at home. So keep your tongue moist with glorifying, praising and declaring His oneness, and give the morning and evening their special adhkar, for they protect your day and illuminate your heart.

en.title: Except If Allah Wills
en.excerpt: Plan for your tomorrow, but make it depend on Allah's will, for you do not control what will be.

body.text: The two verses direct us to a courtesy in speaking about the future: that a person should not say, “I will do such-and-such tomorrow,” without making it conditional on Allah's will; that he should remember his Lord when he forgets; and that he should hope his Lord will guide him to what is nearer to right conduct.

وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَاْيۡءٍ إِنِّي فَاعِلٞ ذَٰلِكَ غَدًا
إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ وَٱذۡكُر رَّبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ وَقُلۡ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَهۡدِيَنِ رَبِّي لِأَقۡرَبَ مِنۡ هَٰذَا رَشَدٗا

Saying “in sha' Allah” (if Allah wills) is not a phrase for evading a promise; it is an acknowledgment that tomorrow is in Allah's hand. So when you resolve on something, plan for it seriously, then make it dependent on your Lord's will, and fulfil what you promised when you are able.

In the words “and remember your Lord when you forget” there is mercy and ease: whoever was heedless and then remembers returns to his Lord without blame. And the verse's closing supplication, “perhaps my Lord will guide me,” teaches you always to ask Allah for what is most right, rather than being content with your own opinion.

en.title: Guard Strictly the Prayers
en.excerpt: Guarding the prayer means performing it on time with a humble, devout heart.

body.text: The command to guard the prayers came in the middle of verses dealing with family matters and divorce, as though the prayer is what guards a person amid the ups and downs and problems of life. It is the constant that does not change, however circumstances change around us.
حَٰفِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلۡوُسۡطَىٰ وَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ

Guarding it includes its time, its form and the heart: that you pray on time, complete the bowing and prostration, and stand before Allah “devoutly obedient,” humble and still. If circumstances become hard for you or problems grow heavy, do not make them a reason to delay your prayer; rather, make your prayer a reason for your worries to lighten, for it is the appointment at which you lay your burdens before Allah.

en.title: We Will Join Their Offspring with Them
en.excerpt: Out of Allah's generosity He reunites the believer with his believing offspring in Paradise, even if their deeds fell short of his rank.

body.text: The verse gives glad tidings to the believers whose offspring followed them in faith: Allah will join their offspring with them in their ranks in Paradise, without reducing anything of the parents' reward. Then it affirms that every person is held in pledge for what he has earned.
وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَاتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُمْ بِإِيمَانٍ أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَمَا أَلَتْنَاهُمْ مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ۚ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينٌ

The family's togetherness does not end with death; whoever raises his children upon faith may hope to be reunited with them in the Home of Honour. This is the greatest incentive for parents to make the soundness of their children's religion their first concern, before their worldly success. And the end of the verse reminds each individual of his responsibility for his own deeds: lineage alone is not enough; one must follow in faith.

en.title: It Is from Allah
en.excerpt: Maryam attributes provision to Allah and declares that Allah provides for whom He wills without measure.

body.text: Maryam (peace be upon her) grew up under the care of Zakariyya (peace be upon him). Whenever he entered upon her in her sanctuary, he found provision with her, and he would ask her in amazement where it came from, and she would answer him with certainty and simplicity. It is a scene that fills the heart with trust in Allah's generosity.

فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنْبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا ۖ كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا الْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِنْدَهَا رِزْقًا ۖ قَالَ يَا مَرْيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَٰذَا ۖ قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ

Provision is in Allah's hand alone, and it may come by ways a person does not expect. Maryam's answer teaches us to attribute every blessing to Allah, so that we are neither deluded by our own means nor despairing when things become tight. The verse also says that Allah accepted her “with a goodly acceptance” and caused her to grow “a goodly growth”; a righteous upbringing in an environment of obedience and worship is among the greatest things a person can be granted, and it is the fruit of a sincere intention and a heartfelt supplication.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 37

en.title: O Soul at Peace
en.excerpt: The soul that found peace through faith in this world is called to its Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing.

body.text: A tender call is addressed to the believing soul: “O soul at peace,” followed by an invitation to return to its Lord, well-pleased with the honour it receives from Him, and well-pleasing to Him for the deeds it sent forth.

يَا أَيَّتُهَا النَّفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ
ارْجِعِي إِلَىٰ رَبِّكِ رَاضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً

The tranquility with which a person's life is sealed by this call is built in this world: through faith, remembrance, contentment with Allah's decree, and righteous deeds. Whoever finds peace in Allah during his life may hope to be called with this call when he meets Him. So plant today what you would love to harvest tomorrow.

Ask yourself: what is unsettling your heart right now, and what could restore it to its peace? Then strive to be content with Allah in what He decrees, for contentment is a path to being one with whom He is pleased.

en.title: Before Death Comes to One of You
en.excerpt: Spend today from what you have been provided, before you wish for a short respite in which to give charity.

body.text: The verse commands spending from what Allah has provided before death comes, when a person will wish he were granted a little more time so he could give charity and be among the righteous. But wishing will not benefit him then, for the time for deeds will have ended.
وَأَنْفِقُوا مِنْ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوْلَا أَخَّرْتَنِي إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ قَرِيبٍ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُنْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ

Notice what the dying person in the verse wishes for: he does not ask for more enjoyment, but for a chance to give charity. What he will wish for tomorrow, you can do today. And reflect on the words “from what We have provided you”: wealth is provision from Allah to begin with, and you are spending from what He gave you. Start with a charity, even a small one; today it is possible, and tomorrow it may not be.

en.title: Do Not Pursue That of Which You Have No Knowledge
en.excerpt: Do not speak or judge except with knowledge, for your hearing, sight and heart will all be questioned.

body.text: The verse forbids following what a person has no knowledge of, whether assumption, rumour or hasty judgment, and reminds us that the hearing, the sight and the heart will each be asked about by their owner. The word, the glance and the assumption are all on the scale.
وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ السَّمْعَ وَالْبَصَرَ وَالْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُولَٰئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْئُولًا

Before you speak about someone or judge them, ask yourself: do I know this for certain? If you do not know, stay silent. This protects your tongue from backbiting and slander, and your heart from suspicion, and makes you worthy of trust. Saying “I don't know” is better than plunging in without knowledge, for which a person will be held to account.

en.title: They Remember Allah and Seek Forgiveness for Their Sins
en.excerpt: The God-conscious are not infallible, but when they err they remember Allah and quickly return to Him.

body.text: The verse describes the God-conscious as those who, when they commit a grave sin or wrong themselves, remember Allah and His greatness, seek forgiveness for their sins, and do not persist in what they have done while they know. And none forgives sins except Allah.

وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُوا فَاحِشَةً أَوْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا لِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَمَنْ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلُوا وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ

What is required is not that you never err, but that you do not persist in error. If you slip, remember your Lord at once, seek forgiveness, and leave the sin; do not remain on it while you know. And remember that the door of forgiveness is with Allah alone, so do not despair of it, and do not look for it anywhere else.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 135

en.title: Indeed, I Am with You Both; I Hear and I See
en.excerpt: When you take a difficult stand for the truth, remember that Allah is with you, hearing and seeing.

body.text: When Allah sent Musa and Harun to Pharaoh and they feared his tyranny, He reassured them, saying: Do not fear; I am with you both with help and support, hearing what is said and seeing what happens. It is reassurance for everyone who stands up for the truth.
قَالَ لَا تَخَافَا ۖ إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ

Fear is human nature, even in prophets, and its cure is not denying it but bringing to mind that Allah is with you. If you dread a situation in which you must speak the truth or face hardship, remember “Indeed, I am with you both,” and go forward with steadfastness and good manners. And seek help through supplication before the situation.

In “I hear and I see” is the reminder that Allah knows all that takes place, so no right is lost with Him and no plot is hidden from Him; be at peace that your affair is within His hearing and sight. Whoever keeps this nearness of Allah in mind will neither overstep the truth in his words nor retreat from it out of fear of people.

en.title: Charity by Which You Purify Them and Cause Them to Grow
en.excerpt: Charity purifies the soul of stinginess and makes it grow in goodness, even before it benefits the poor.

body.text: This verse mentions two effects of charity on the soul of the giver: a purification that removes the stinginess and sins clinging to the heart, and a growth that increases goodness and blessing in it. The giver is the first to benefit.
خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِمْ بِهَا وَصَلِّ عَلَيْهِمْ ۖ إِنَّ صَلَاتَكَ سَكَنٌ لَهُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ

So do not see charity as a loss from your wealth; it is a cure for your heart's attachment to the world, and an increase in your wealth through Allah's blessing. The verse also mentions that the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for those who gave charity was a source of tranquility for them. So when you give to someone in need, do not think yourself above needing their prayers, and when someone gives to you, pray for them, for supplication brings comfort to hearts.

en.title: Sons and Grandchildren
en.excerpt: Children and grandchildren are an ever-renewing blessing that deserves gratitude and care.

body.text: The verse lists among Allah's blessings that He made for people spouses from among themselves, and made for them from their spouses sons and grandchildren, and provided them with good things. Then it censures those who are ungrateful for Allah's blessing.

وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ بَنِينَ وَحَفَدَةً وَرَزَقَكُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ ۚ أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ وَبِنِعْمَتِ اللَّهِ هُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ

The extension of the family across generations is a great blessing: grandchildren renew joy in the home and connect the generations to one another. Part of being grateful for this blessing is that grandparents and parents take care to pass on values and faith, and that grandchildren take care to honour their grandparents and visit them, so that the family remains a tree whose roots and branches are connected.

en.title: Shake the Trunk of the Palm Tree Toward You
en.excerpt: Despite her weakness, Maryam was told to shake the trunk; taking means does not contradict reliance on Allah.

body.text: In a moment of pain and loneliness, Maryam (peace be upon her) is commanded to shake the trunk of the palm tree so that fresh ripe dates will fall upon her, even though a palm trunk is not usually shaken by a weak and weary hand.
وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا

Allah was able to make the dates fall without any movement from her, but He commanded her to do what she could, and then He took charge of the result. This is the balance of reliance on Allah: that you exert what is within your capacity and leave what is not in your hand to Allah. So do not belittle your small effort when facing something great. Do what you are able to do sincerely, for blessing comes from Allah, and He may place much good in your modest striving.

en.title: So When You Are Free, Strive Hard
en.excerpt: The believer moves from one good deed to another and directs all his longing toward his Lord.

body.text: The surah closes with two short directions: when you have finished one task, exert yourself in the worship of your Lord, and make your longing and aim toward Allah alone. There is no free time in a believer's life that should go to waste.

فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَانْصَبْ
وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَارْغَبْ

Free time is a blessing if it is filled with good, and a door to slackness if it is left without direction. The verse teaches that rest should be a transition from one effort to another, not a break from the goal. So fill your time with what benefits you in your religion and your worldly life.

Placing “to your Lord” before “direct your longing” conveys that longing should be for Him alone, so let your goal in everything you do be Allah's pleasure. When you finish your daily tasks, take your share of remembrance, supplication or recitation.

en.title: Hasten to Forgiveness from Your Lord
en.excerpt: Forgiveness and Paradise deserve haste, not procrastination and delay.

body.text: The verse commands hastening toward two great things: forgiveness from Allah, and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-conscious. The command to hasten indicates the greatness of what is sought and the shortness of the time available to attain it.
وَسَارِعُوا إِلَىٰ مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ

Procrastination is among the greatest things that block a servant's path: I will repent tomorrow, I will start once I'm free, I will reform when things calm down. The verse says: hasten. So choose one good deed and begin it now, and do not wait for perfect circumstances. And reflect on how forgiveness is mentioned before Paradise: purification from sins is the way to entering it.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 133

en.title: Do Not Put in Our Hearts Any Resentment
en.excerpt: A heart free of rancour is a blessing to be sought from Allah through supplication.

body.text: The verse describes those who came after the forerunners as praying for their brothers' forgiveness and asking Allah not to put in their hearts any rancour toward the believers. A heart free of resentment does not come about automatically; it is something sought from Allah.

وَالَّذِينَ جَاءُوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَلِإِخْوَانِنَا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِالْإِيمَانِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلًّا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ رَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ

If you find in your chest a tightness or envy toward someone, do not surrender to it. Instead, ask Allah to purify your heart, and pray for good for that person, for praying for others is among the strongest cures for rancour. Make this supplication a regular practice, for a sound heart is ease in this world and provision for the Hereafter.

en.title: Remember Your Lord Within Yourself, Humbly and in Awe
en.excerpt: The etiquette of remembrance: humility, earnest pleading and a low voice, morning and evening, without heedlessness.

body.text: At the close of Surah Al-A'raf, Allah guides His Prophet ﷺ and the believers to remember Him within themselves with humility and fear, in a low voice without raising it, at the beginning and end of the day, and forbids them from being among those heedless of His remembrance.
وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ فِى نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعًۭا وَخِيفَةًۭ وَدُونَ ٱلْجَهْرِ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ بِٱلْغُدُوِّ وَٱلْءَاصَالِ وَلَا تَكُن مِّنَ ٱلْغَٰفِلِينَ

Remembrance is not words repeated without presence of heart; it is the heart's conversation with its Lord. So remember Allah with humility and a calm voice, bring to mind His greatness and mercy, and be especially keen on the morning and evening adhkar. Heedlessness is the most dangerous thing that can afflict the heart, and constant remembrance is its greatest cure.

en.title: No! Indeed, My Lord Is with Me; He Will Guide Me
en.excerpt: The sea before them and the enemy behind them, and the word was: No! My Lord is with me.

body.text: When the two hosts, of Musa and of Pharaoh, saw each other, Musa's companions said, “We are surely overtaken!” He answered them with confidence and certainty: No! Indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me to the way of deliverance. That word became an everlasting lesson in trusting Allah.

فَلَمَّا تَرَٰٓءَا ٱلْجَمْعَانِ قَالَ أَصْحَٰبُ مُوسَىٰٓ إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ
قَالَ كَلَّآ ۖ إِنَّ مَعِىَ رَبِّى سَيَهْدِينِ

By outward calculation, being overtaken was imminent, but Musa's certainty rose above calculations, so he said, “No! Indeed, my Lord is with me.” If the doors appear closed in your eyes, do not hand your heart over to despair; renew your trust that Allah opens from where you do not expect.

Notice that he did not know how deliverance would come, but he was certain that it would come: “He will guide me.” Such is certainty: to trust Allah even if you do not yet see the way, while continuing to walk. Certainty does not cancel effort; it gives it strength and patience.

en.title: Then Do Not Follow What They Spend with Reminders or Hurt
en.excerpt: Noble giving is not followed by reminders of favour or by hurt; otherwise its blessing is lost.

body.text: This verse praises those who spend in the way of Allah and then do not follow their giving by reminding the recipient of their favour, nor by hurt in word or treatment. Their reward is kept safe with their Lord.
ٱلَّذِينَ يُنفِقُونَ أَمۡوَٰلَهُمۡ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ لَا يُتۡبِعُونَ مَآ أَنفَقُواْ مَنّٗا وَلَآ أَذٗى لَّهُمۡ أَجۡرُهُمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ

How many a good charity has been spoiled by a tongue that talks about it too much, or by a look of superiority toward the one who took it! True giving is to forget what you gave and to preserve the dignity of the one you gave to. Keep your charity a secret between you and Allah as much as you can, so that you attain what the verse promised: a reward with the Lord, safety from fear, and freedom from grief.

en.title: Then Speak to Them a Gentle Word
en.excerpt: If you find nothing to give, do not deny the one who asks a gentle word that mends his heart.

body.text: The verse speaks of someone who turns away from giving to a relative or a needy person because he finds nothing to give, while awaiting provision he hopes for from Allah. It commands him to speak to them a gentle, easy word.
وَإِمَّا تُعْرِضَنَّ عَنْهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ رَحْمَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكَ تَرْجُوهَا فَقُلْ لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَيْسُورًا

Not everyone is able to give at every time, but everyone is able to offer a kind word: a sincere promise, a good prayer, or a gentle apology. If a brother or relative asks you for help you do not have, do not wound him with a curt reply; rather, speak to him a gentle word that preserves his dignity and keeps the affection between you.

en.title: Even If It Be the Weight of a Mustard Seed
en.excerpt: Luqman teaches his son that Allah encompasses the smallest and most hidden deeds, so nothing is lost with Him.

body.text: Luqman gives his son advice that fills the heart with awareness of Allah's watchfulness: that a deed, however small, even the weight of a mustard seed, and however hidden, whether in a rock, in the heavens or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth.
يَا بُنَيَّ إِنَّهَا إِنْ تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ فَتَكُنْ فِي صَخْرَةٍ أَوْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ أَوْ فِي الْأَرْضِ يَأْتِ بِهَا اللَّهُ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ

This advice builds within the soul an inner watchfulness that needs no human overseer. When a person knows that Allah is “Subtle, All-Aware,” he feels shy of sinning in private, and is reassured that his hidden good deeds are preserved. Do not belittle any good deed or any sin, for the small kind word and the small harm are both recorded. This drives us to perfect our work and to correct our intention, in private and in public.

en.title: Do Not Weaken and Do Not Grieve, for You Will Be Uppermost
en.excerpt: Faith raises the believer above weakness and grief, even when wounds and defeats befall him.

body.text: This verse was revealed to console the believers after what had befallen them. It forbade them from weakness and grief and reminded them that they are uppermost as long as they are believers. True elevation is measured by faith, not by the outcome of a moment.
وَلَا تَهِنُوا وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ

A believer may stumble in his work or his life, but the verse teaches him not to let stumbling break his spirit, and to remember that his worth with Allah lies in his faith and steadfastness, not in a passing success that eludes him. The believer is strong through his Lord, even if his means are weak.

If failure befalls you, acknowledge the pain, but do not give in to weakness. Rise again, review your means, and hold fast to your faith, for in the words “if you are believers” lies the key to lasting honour. True honour does not vanish with a passing loss.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 139

en.title: They Call upon Their Lord in Fear and Hope
en.excerpt: The believer's heart travels to Allah on two wings: fear of His punishment and hope in His mercy.

body.text: The verse describes servants whose sides forsake their beds: they give up the pleasure of sleep to call upon their Lord, fearing His punishment and hoping for His reward, and they spend in good causes from what Allah has provided them.
تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَضَاجِعِ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ

The verse combines fear and hope. Fear alone may lead to despair, and hope alone may lead to complacency, but together they keep the heart balanced. In the night prayer, even a few rak'ahs, there is a solitude that brings these two meanings together for you, so set for yourself a fixed share of it that you keep up.

en.title: And Whoever Is Patient and Forgives
en.excerpt: Patience with harm, together with forgiveness, is among the highest degrees of character.

body.text: The verse praises the one who combines two things: patience with harm and forgiveness of the wrongdoer, and describes this as being among the matters requiring resolve, that is, matters that need strong determination and sincere will, which only the great are capable of.
وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ

Patience alone may leave bitterness in the heart, but patience together with forgiveness purifies the heart completely. If you are harmed, first be patient and do not take revenge, then forgive so that no trace of the offence remains in your soul. This does not mean always giving up your right; it means choosing the nobler path when pardon is more beneficial.

en.title: Allah Is Sufficient for Us, and He Is the Best Disposer of Affairs
en.excerpt: A phrase that turns fear into faith: the believers said it when they were frightened with people, and it only increased their steadfastness.

body.text: The verse describes believers who were told that people had gathered great forces against them, so they should fear them. This intimidation only increased them in faith and steadfastness, and they said with confident hearts: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best One in whom to place our trust.
الَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ فَاخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَانًا وَقَالُوا حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ

When you are surrounded by fears and threats, or people keep trying to frighten you, return to this phrase. It means that Allah suffices you against what concerns you, and that He is the best One to whom matters can be entrusted. Say it with certainty, take the means, and leave the results to your Lord.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 173

en.title: To Allah Belong the Most Beautiful Names, So Call upon Him by Them
en.excerpt: Each of Allah's names is a door to supplication, so call upon Him by the name that suits your need.

body.text: The verse affirms that to Allah belong the most beautiful names, commands calling upon Him by them, and forbids following those who deviate from the truth concerning His names, for they will be recompensed for what they used to do. It is a verse that combines making Allah known with guidance on how to call upon Him.
وَلِلَّهِ ٱلْأَسْمَآءُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ فَٱدْعُوهُ بِهَا ۖ وَذَرُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ فِىٓ أَسْمَٰٓئِهِۦ ۚ سَيُجْزَوْنَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ

The command “so call upon Him by them” opens a practical door in supplication: if you seek forgiveness, call upon Him as the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful; if you seek provision, call upon Him as the Provider, the Most Generous; if you seek healing, call upon Him as the Healer. Thus your supplication combines request and praise together.

Knowing the most beautiful names increases faith; whenever you learn a name and reflect on its meaning, your love for your Lord and your awareness of Him increase. So set aside a share for learning their meanings, and repeat them in your supplication with a present heart, for calling upon Him by them is worship and knowledge at once.

en.title: Men Whom Neither Trade nor Sale Distracts
en.excerpt: The people of the mosques work and trade, but the world does not distract them from the remembrance of Allah.

body.text: These two verses describe the houses of Allah which He has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned, where He is glorified morning and evening. Then they praise men who frequent them: neither trade nor sale distracts them from the remembrance of Allah, establishing prayer and giving zakah.

فِي بُيُوتٍ أَذِنَ اللَّهُ أَنْ تُرْفَعَ وَيُذْكَرَ فِيهَا اسْمُهُ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ
رِجَالٌ لَا تُلْهِيهِمْ تِجَارَةٌ وَلَا بَيْعٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَإِقَامِ الصَّلَاةِ وَإِيتَاءِ الزَّكَاةِ ۙ يَخَافُونَ يَوْمًا تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ الْقُلُوبُ وَالْأَبْصَارُ

The verse did not praise those who abandoned trade, but those whom trade did not distract. The believer works and earns, but his heart is attached to the call to prayer; when the time of prayer comes, he leaves what is in his hand. So set limits on your work by which you protect your prayer, and remember that these men “fear a Day” in which hearts will be overturned; their fear led them to put the Hereafter first.

en.title: Peace Be upon You; I Will Ask My Lord to Forgive You
en.excerpt: Ibrahim's reply to his angry father is a model of a son's courtesy toward his father, however severe the disagreement.

body.text: After Azar threatened his son Ibrahim and ordered him to leave him, Ibrahim did not respond with anger. Instead he said, “Peace be upon you,” and promised to ask his Lord to forgive him, explaining that Allah had always been gracious to him.
قَالَ سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكَ ۖ سَأَسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّي ۖ إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِي حَفِيًّا

Disagreement with a parent does not justify harshness. Ibrahim held firm to the truth, yet he bid his father farewell with peace, gentleness and prayer. When you encounter severity or misunderstanding from your parents, make your response one of peace, and do not let anger take you out of dutifulness; your gentleness may be the door that opens their hearts one day.

en.title: Leave It in Its Ears
en.excerpt: In Yusuf's interpretation of the dream is a wise plan for saving and sound management in times of plenty.

body.text: Yusuf (peace be upon him) interprets the king's dream, and he does not stop at explaining it; he offers a practical plan: diligent farming for seven years, storing the harvest in its ears, and economy in eating, in preparation for hard years to come.

قَالَ تَزْرَعُونَ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ دَأَبًا فَمَا حَصَدْتُمْ فَذَرُوهُ فِي سُنْبُلِهِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ
ثُمَّ يَأْتِي مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ سَبْعٌ شِدَادٌ يَأْكُلْنَ مَا قَدَّمْتُمْ لَهُنَّ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِمَّا تُحْصِنُونَ

It is wise for a person to prepare in days of plenty for days of hardship. Yusuf guided them to eat “a little of what you eat” and store the rest, and this planning was, by Allah's permission, the cause of the people being saved from famine.

This is a practical lesson in managing money at home and at work: to work hard, to be economical in spending, and to save something for the future. Planning does not contradict reliance on Allah; it is part of taking the means that Allah has commanded.

en.title: Placing “You Alone” First in Al-Fatihah
en.excerpt: Placing the pronoun before the verb restricts worship and seeking help to Allah alone.

body.text: A verse that the Muslim repeats in every rak'ah, combining the purpose of creation and its means: worshipping Allah and seeking His help. Its wording carries subtle meanings worth pausing over, so reflect on it in your next prayer with a present heart.
إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ

A subtle insight in the order of the words: the pronoun “You alone” (iyyaka) was placed before the two verbs. Had it been said “we worship You and we seek Your help,” it would not have conveyed exclusivity; with the pronoun placed first, the meaning is: we worship none but You, and we seek help from none but You. Then “You alone” was repeated with each verb to stress that each of them is reserved for Allah independently. This is among the most eloquent expressions of tawhid in the shortest phrase.

Worship was placed before seeking help because worship is the goal and seeking help is a means to it. It also indicates that the servant cannot carry out worship except with Allah's help: he declares his direction, then asks for support. How much we need to bring this meaning to mind in every rak'ah!

en.title: What Has Deceived You Concerning Your Lord, the Most Generous?
en.excerpt: Why did the description “the Most Generous” come in the context of reproach? To awaken shyness in the heart, not complacency.

body.text: The verses address man reproachfully: what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Most Generous, so that you fell short in His right? Then they remind him of the blessing of being created, proportioned and balanced, and assembled in whatever form Allah willed for him.

يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ
الَّذِي خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ
فِي أَيِّ صُورَةٍ مَا شَاءَ رَكَّبَكَ

A subtle insight in choosing the description “your Lord, the Most Generous” here: the reproach is joined to generosity, as if the meaning were: how can you meet generosity with negligence? Allah's giving the servant respite and concealing his faults is no reason for complacency, but for shyness before Him. Then it follows with the mention of creating, proportioning and balancing, so that the prior kindness bears witness to the right of the Giver of blessings.

en.title: And They Prefer Others over Themselves
en.excerpt: Preferring others despite one's own need is the peak of generosity that Allah praised.

body.text: The verse describes the people of Madinah who received their emigrant brothers with love: they find in their chests no envy for what the emigrants were given, but rather prefer them over themselves, even if they themselves are in severe need.

وَالَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُوا الدَّارَ وَالْإِيمَانَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ يُحِبُّونَ مَنْ هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ حَاجَةً مِمَّا أُوتُوا وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَىٰ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ خَصَاصَةٌ ۚ وَمَنْ يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ

A subtle insight in the words “even though they are in privation”: preferring others when one is wealthy is easy, but doing so in need and poverty is true heroism. The verb in “they prefer others over themselves” came in the present tense to indicate that it is a constantly renewed habit, not a passing act. Then it closes with “and whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul” in the passive voice, indicating that being saved from stinginess is a success granted by Allah, so it is to be sought from Him.

en.title: And Glorify Him Through a Long Night
en.excerpt: Reflect on how glorification at night is described as long, while the day is mentioned only by its two ends.

body.text: Allah commands His Prophet ﷺ to remember His name at the beginning and end of the day, then to prostrate to Him during part of the night, and to glorify Him through a long night, thus combining remembrance, prostration and glorification across all the times of the day.

وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا
وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَاسْجُدْ لَهُ وَسَبِّحْهُ لَيْلًا طَوِيلًا

A subtle insight in how the times are distributed: the day is mentioned by its two ends, “morning and evening,” because it is the time of striving and work, while the night is singled out for prostration, and glorification in it is described as “through a long night,” for the night is the time of solitude and calm that has room for intimate supplication. So give your day remembrance at its beginning and end, and give your night a longer share of prayer and glorification, even a few rak'ahs that you keep up consistently.

en.title: And on the Earth Are Signs for Those with Certainty
en.excerpt: Certainty is built through reflection: on the earth around you, and on your own self within you.

body.text: The two verses draw attention to the signs of Allah's power on the earth, with its mountains, seas, plants and animals, signs from which those with certainty benefit; and then to His signs within people themselves: will you not then see?

وَفِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ ءَايَٰتٞ لِّلۡمُوقِنِينَ
وَفِيٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ

The words “and within yourselves” make the nearest of signs to you your own self: your heartbeat, your breathing, your senses. Take a moment to reflect on how you were created, for that increases certainty and gives rise to gratitude. Whoever reflects on himself sees enough signs of divine power.

The signs are specified as being “for those with certainty” to show that it is the prepared heart that benefits from what it sees. So ask Allah for certainty that lets you see in every created thing evidence of its Creator. Do not pass by familiar sights as the heedless do; pause at them in reflection.

en.title: Indeed, the First House Established for Mankind
en.excerpt: The Ka'bah is the first house established for the worship of Allah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.

body.text: This verse introduces the Sacred House: it is the first house established for mankind for the worship of Allah, and it is blessed and a guidance for the worlds. It is the qiblah of the Muslims and the place their hearts yearn for wherever they are, and toward it faces turn in every prayer.
إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ مُبَارَكًا وَهُدًى لِلْعَالَمِينَ

Your turning toward the Ka'bah in every prayer connects you to this ancient history of tawhid, and unites you with millions of worshippers who face a single qiblah. So when you face the qiblah, bring to mind that you are turning toward a house that is “blessed and a guidance,” and ask Allah to grant you a visit to it, and to give you a share of its guidance and blessing even if you live far away.

sources: The Holy Qur'an — Surah Al Imran: 96

en.title: Whether You Eat Together or Separately
en.excerpt: The homes of relatives and friends are open with affection, and the greeting in them is a blessing and goodness.

body.text: The verse lifts blame from those with excuses, and from eating in the homes of fathers and mothers, brothers and sisters, paternal and maternal uncles and aunts, and friends, whether together or separately. Then it commands greeting with peace upon entering homes, a greeting blessed and good.

لَيْسَ عَلَى الْأَعْمَىٰ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى الْأَعْرَجِ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَى الْمَرِيضِ حَرَجٌ وَلَا عَلَىٰ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ آبَائِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ إِخْوَانِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخَوَاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَعْمَامِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ عَمَّاتِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ أَخْوَالِكُمْ أَوْ بُيُوتِ خَالَاتِكُمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكْتُمْ مَفَاتِحَهُ أَوْ صَدِيقِكُمْ ۚ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَأْكُلُوا جَمِيعًا أَوْ أَشْتَاتًا ۚ فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُمْ بُيُوتًا فَسَلِّمُوا عَلَىٰ أَنْفُسِكُمْ تَحِيَّةً مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ مُبَارَكَةً طَيِّبَةً ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ
